items.statement: Plans to open 25 to 30 new stores in FY25, with EBOs central to growth strategy
items.quote: We are optimistic about our continued store expansion efforts and aim to open between 25 to 30 new stores this year during FY '25.

items.statement: Expects to maintain EBITDA margin between 28% to 30%
items.quote: EBITDA margin also as we have said in the earlier calls we expect to maintain between 28 % to 30%.

items.statement: Gross margins will remain around 58% level
items.quote: I think last year we did a little north of 56 -odd crores as a gross margin -- 57-odd crores and this year we've done -- 58-odd percentage I'm sorry not crores . So gross margins will remain there and thereabouts .

items.statement: Plans to spend approximately 5% of revenues on branding and advertising for the full year
items.quote: For the full year, we plan to spend approximately 5% of revenues on branding and a dvertising.

items.statement: Market for premium and mid-premium branded apparel continued to be subdued due to inflationary environment and nationwide heat wave
items.quote: The market for premium and mid -premium branded apparel conti nued to be subdued due to the consumer behaviour influenced by an inflationary environment and a nationwide heat wave we experienced this summer.

items.statement: Hoping festival season and marriage season pick up well after elections and stable prices
items.quote: we are hoping that the festiva l season and the marriage season should pick up well and we should have a good season.

items.quote: Maybe 2%-odd. It does not necessarily reflect price escalation it also reflects the product mix the ratio of what else and as we are going toward premiumization there might be some premium products that get added etcetera and that may take up prices.

items.statement: Market conditions remain volatile and difficult to predict; not putting gun to head to grow at any pace but focusing on profitability and same-store sales growth
items.quote: Given that it's very difficult to look into the crysta l ball today and gaze there and give an exact idea of what will happen , but we are very positive and hopeful and hoping now that the elections also are behind us and prices have been stable now for all the last few seasons so we are hoping that the festiva l season and the marriage season should pick up well and we should have a good season.

items.statement: Working capital days decreased by 5 days to 161 days as of 30 June 2024; aims to reduce by another 5-7 days by year-end
items.quote: Business we are in, in retail we need -- I mean that does not give an absolute true reflection of how the brand is doing. But give or take five, seven days here or there

items.quote: Why not certainly we intend to you know double in four to five years is what we had mentioned earlier also however all of that will be done depending on the market conditions and we have always grown the through the profitability lens and that is something we will continue to do we will calibrate the growth of the through the profitability lens.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth for Q1 FY25 stood at 3% year-on-year

items.statement: Added five new stores in Q1 FY25, increasing total store count to 430
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, we added fi ve new stores to our portfolio, increasing our total strength of stores to 430.

items.statement: Provision for returns increased to 25% from 22% last year due to shift to SOR basis from outright
items.quote: last year in Q1 the provision for returns was 22% and this year the provision for returns has been consistent 25 % as per the provision made in Q4 of last year.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue growth guidance of 25% to 30% alongside anticipated margin improvement
items.quote: Finally, we are pleased to reaffirm our guidance of 25%, 30% revenue growth for FY '25 alongside an anticipated improvement in our margin profiles.

items.statement: Long-term sales growth guidance of 25% to 30% year-on-year for a longer period
items.quote: Our long -term guidance to the market for sales growth will be in the range of 25% to 30% on a year -on-year basis for a longer period of time.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance range of 33% to 36% depending on product and sector mix
items.quote: Our long -term guidance to the market for EBITDA margins will be in the range of 33% to 36%, depending upon product and sector mix.

items.statement: Order book stands at over Rs. 3,300 crores, up from Rs. 2,000 crores a few quarters earlier
items.quote: Our order book has skyrocketed from Rs. 2,000 crores a few quarters earlier to over Rs. 3,300 crores today, driven by strategic contracts and key customer acquisitions

items.statement: New facility 10x existing size on track to be ready by FY26 with high visibility on first phase utilization
items.quote: We are on track to complete the expansion phase and will be ready by and from FY '26. With orders in hand and pipeline of validations, we have high visibility on the utilization of the first phase.

items.statement: Aerospace and Defense contributed ~19% of Q1 FY25 revenue, in line with diversification plan
items.quote: During the quarter, Aerospace and Defense contributed around 19% of our total revenue, which is in line with our long -term diversification plan.

items.statement: GTRE/DRDO order for complete turbojet engine assembly marks entry into propulsion systems as single-source industry partner
items.quote: An order from GTRE/DRDO for manufacturing and assembly of a turbojet engine. Now, this is a very, very exciting opportunity and this is going to take Azad into a very different league.

items.quote: A seven-year contract with Rolls-Royce for the Defense and military aircraft engines. Two major contracts from Baker Hughes. A contract from GE Vernova for supply of high -complex rotating airfoils for the Nuclear, industrial, and thermal power industries.

items.quote: Likewise, we have added a subsidiary Azad VTC, for special processes and coatings, which will help us reduce job work charge as well as the dependency.

items.quote: On the account of that, we have acquired a company, VTC, where we started qualifying for those particular process es. And going forward, we see that this cost will normalize again.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 240 crores primary capital for FY27 infrastructure and capacity deployment; now planning CAPEX beyond FY27 given contract wins
items.quote: And for FY '27 we had raised a primary of Rs. 240 crores and this was to be deployed towards infrastructure and capacity. And now, we are planning how do we go beyond FY '27 ?

items.statement: Targeting INR 1,000 crore revenue for FY25 with 18% EBITDA margin; Q1 behind but confident to get close
items.quote: That's the objective, Prathik. Q1, we are a little behind. We are hopeful we can make it up. The whole idea is if you aim big, you will get close to the target. So it's an aggressive goal but as of now, at the end of Q1, we are confident that we'll get close to it, if not at it.

items.statement: Revenue gap of INR 150 crore to reach INR 1,000 crore target including Augmento; weighted pipeline INR 50 crore
items.quote: If I look at our pipeline today, Vikas and our order book, we have from a INR 1,000 crores, we have a gap of INR 150 crores. This is including Augmento.

items.statement: Unweighted pipeline INR 150 crore, weighted pipeline INR 50 crore to close revenue gap
items.quote: So the un-weighted pipeline would be INR 150 crores, but the weighted pipeline would be in the range of INR 50 crores.

items.statement: Digital engineering contributes 45% of revenue, QA/testing 15%, balance data and infrastructure
items.quote: So Amit, digital engineering, which is a product capability, that shows almost 45% of our revenues. The QA and the testing, that's about 15% and the balance comes between data and infrastructure.

items.statement: Augmento Labs acquired June 2024; expected INR 50 crore revenue in FY25 at 20%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: Approximately INR 50 crores.

items.statement: Augmento expected to deliver at least 20% EBITDA margin, above company average
items.quote: Yes, 20% at least. At least.

items.statement: High technology spend in Fintech, Hi-Tech, and Retail e-commerce verticals driving growth
items.quote: Technology spend today globally is moving I mean, is increasing in these business verticals, in these verticals. So the ability for us to grow becomes better because we have targeted high growth areas.

items.statement: Fintech startup clients pose payment risk due to funding-dependent spending patterns
items.quote: What we have to be careful about is, and this is a fine line that we have to ride is, since a lot of these are startups, we have to be careful that w e don't get stuck with them

items.statement: Utilization at 85%, expected to remain flat with 100-200 bps variation
items.quote: I think this is pretty much maxed out. Maybe 100-200 basis points in either direction is probably what you will see, but 85% is pretty much where we will remain.

items.statement: Hired 3 salespeople in US (2 in June) and 1 in UK (June) to drive US revenue mix toward 45-75%
items.quote: We have hired 3 new sales guys in the U.S. 1 is the guy who brought this Hi-tech company and this was 7 months ago, and 2 have joined in the month of June.

items.statement: Augmento integration painless; support functions integrating, delivery teams folded into Hi-Tech vertical
items.quote: So I would say, so far no surprises, quite a painless integration.

items.statement: No focus on HealthTech/MedTech; sector parked for now
items.quote: Correct. That didn't work out. And, I think this is a sector, which we are sort of parked, not going to focus on it excessively for now.

items.statement: Future acquisitions limited to small capability players due to capital constraints
items.quote: We're always talking to potential targets, hopeful something will come out. But, you know, we don't have that much money with us now to make a big play.

items.statement: Billing rate improvement dependent on rupee-dollar movement
items.quote: One big area they'll come from is our finance minister, if the rupee dollar benefits.

items.statement: DSO increased marginally to 65 days; no significant collection issues
items.quote: Marginal I think, Niraj is saying it's a marginal increase.

items.statement: Targeting breakeven in Jeevansathi this year with high growth and aggressive monetization
items.quote: So, in Jeevansathi we are targeting breakeven this year. So we would like to get as close to breakeven as possible.

items.statement: Targeting breakeven or profit in Shiksha this year while investing in platform and content
items.quote: In Shiksha, can we continue to be profitable? The domestic business grew very well in Q1. Study abroad is struggling a little bit because of what we're seeing are happening around the world. So even in Shiksha, we would want to at least, target breakeven or make make some profit this year.

items.statement: Willing to invest more in 99acres even if it means taking losses for longer to capture long-term opportunity
items.quote: We would want 99acres to grow faster going forward. We are doing whatever we can and if that requires us to invest a lot more in the business, and if that means taking a loss of some more time, that's fine with us.

items.statement: Continuing to invest in recruitment verticals including JobHai, AmbitionBox, iimjobs, hirist and Naukri Gulf
items.quote: Even in recruitment, we will continue, we continue to invest in our JobHai business. We continue to invest behind the AmbitionBox platform. We continue to invest behind iimjob and hirist. Even our Naukri Gulf business has been doing well, We continue to invest in the business.

items.statement: Gestation projects in recruitment verticals costing Rs. 20-25 crores per quarter
items.quote: In the range, you said, Rs. 20-25 crores a quarter, around that much.

items.statement: 99acres advertising spend higher than last year; manpower costs under control
items.quote: We are actually spending more than we spent last year. I don't know exactly how much. Right now, as we speak, we have a higher budget than we spent last year. On the other hand manpower costs, etc. are under control.

items.statement: IT hiring showing early recovery signs with July Jobspeak up 12% YoY and 11% MoM; some large IT clients renewed and upgraded
items.quote: The July 2024 Jobspeak report has also been very encouraging. The Jobspeak index grew by 12% Y-o-Y in July and M-o-M grew by 11%.

items.statement: Non-IT billing growth at 14% YoY driven by healthcare, infrastructure, transport, real estate, media & telecom
items.quote: Growth momentum in the Non-IT segment continued, with billings growing at 14% year on year. This was largely driven by sectors such as healthcare and life sciences, infrastructure, transport, real estate and media & telecom.

items.statement: Niche verticals iimjobs, NaukriGulf, Naukri Fast Forward grew billings 26%, 25%, 29% YoY respectively
items.quote: Our niche and adjacent business verticals, including iimjobs, NaukriGulf, and Naukri Fast Forward also maintained healthy billings growth with Y-o-Y increases of 26%, 25%, and 29%, respectively.

items.statement: JobHai expanding to ~60 cities with product-market fit; freemium model targeting 1M SME customers in 5-7 years; monetization started few months ago
items.quote: We've worked very hard on the product for the last three years. And we seem to have got product market fit. There's a lot of traction. We're getting a lot of job seekers, we're getting a lot of jobs. We're getting a lot of recruiters advertising on the platform. And it's a freemium model.

items.statement: 99acres growth hit in June possibly due to election uncertainty; state government changes delaying project approvals
items.quote: Now, again, anecdotally, what I can tell you, the business took a hit in June. Maybe again, it had to do with some uncertainty around the elections. And often when state governments change and all these things happen in real estate some of the projects get delayed. Approvals take longer as people adjust to the new environment.

items.statement: No plan to exit Zomato or Policybazaar holdings; taking long-term view on value creation
items.quote: As of now, there is no plan to exit.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 20% for FY25 maintained but management is cautiously optimistic
items.quote: I would still do not want to jump into any change in numbers, but we are quite cautious and we keep ourselves cautiously optimistic on this year's performance.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs. 16.9 billion as of June 2024 with 63% international and 37% domestic
items.quote: In terms of order book, it stood at Rs. 16.9 billion as of June '24. Out of which, 63% of orders are from international business and the rest 37% are domestic orders.

items.statement: Capex of approximately Rs. 4,500 million planned for FY25 towards brownfield expansion
items.quote: We are looking at a CAPEX of approximately Rs. Rs. 4,500 million during FY '25. This is towards brownfield expansion projects for which we are looking at our existing facilities.

items.statement: Special process facility for aerospace approved with Rs. 30 crore investment, operational by mid-FY26
items.quote: So, this would mean that in over 12 to 15 months, this facility will come up adjacent to our existing machining facility, and this would have an overall investment of about Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded ~200 bps YoY to 41.8% in Q1 FY25 due to favorable product mix
items.quote: During this quarter, the gross margin grew from 39.9% in Q1 of FY '24 to 41.8% in the Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Targeting 20% EBITDA margin through mix improvement, Sweden turnaround, 2-wheeler premiumization and operating leverage
items.quote: These factors aided with the operating leverage on better capacity utilization on various product lines will actually help us to achieve or get closer to the 20% goal of operating margin.

items.statement: Emerging segments (non-auto, tech-agnostic, xEV) grew 34% YoY; tech-agnostic up 68% to Rs. 712M, xEV up 29% to Rs. 421M
items.quote: Together, these segments have expanded by 34% on a year-on-year basis during this quarter. We have registered a top line of Rs. 712 million in auto tech-agnostic products with a year-on-year growth of 68%. Our xEV business grew by 29% on a year-on-year basis to Rs. 421 million

items.statement: Aerospace revenue growth target 30-35% for FY25 (base Rs. 110 crore); exports from India grew ~28% YoY in Q1
items.quote: For this year, for Aerospace, we are looking at between 30% to 35% growth as it stands today.

items.statement: Swedish subsidiary EBITDA margin to reach 12-13% from next financial year with two new engine program wins
items.quote: we have worked, and we have acquired 2 key business wins for our Swedish subsidiary, which will enable us to go back to 12% to 13% EBITDA starting from next financial year.

items.statement: Non-auto, tech-agnostic and xEV segments targeting 40-50% CAGR over next 2-3 years
items.quote: we are looking at a CAGR growth in this by about 40% to 50%.

items.statement: International business outlook slightly worrisome for H2 FY25 due to global slowdown concerns
items.quote: While I would be cautious to say that international business is looking in the second half of this year, especially the international business looks to be slightly worrisome.

items.statement: MOU signed with Karnataka government for 55 acres land for future greenfield expansion
items.quote: we have recently signed an MOU with the government of Karnataka to acquire 55 acres of land. Over the years, we will be looking at greenfield expansion in the area of our current expertise in this piece of land.

items.statement: Aluminum forging production reaching ~1.5 million parts this year; margins in line with domestic products but still on learning curve
items.quote: This year, we will be doing almost close to 1.5 million aluminum parts, which is quite a good progress given the fact that this has been only about 2.5, 3 years of this thing.

items.statement: MMRFIC radar business EBITDA margins expected upwards of 50% upon full integration and field testing
items.quote: generally speaking, the average, the EBITDA numbers on this business would be upwards of 50%.

items.statement: Off-road segment growth to moderate to ~14-15% in FY25 after 66-67% growth in FY24
items.quote: Yes, it may be in that range.

items.statement: Full year FY25 expected to be flattish with Q2 sequentially flat, H2 higher than H1, and Q4 highest run rate; full year could be flat to minus 2-3%
items.quote: I would think the full year outlook would be more flattish for this year. I expect maybe quarter 2 to be sequentially flat. And the half 2 probably -- the second half would be higher than half 1. And with quarter 4, I expect to have the highest run rate.

items.statement: Full year FY25 EBITDA margin target of 18%, long-term target remains 20%
items.quote: But 18% is what I'm looking at for this full year. But my longer-term stand on the 20% margin remains because right now, it's basically the operating leverage causes an issue is when the volumes are down.

items.statement: Capex outlook for FY25 between INR35 crores to INR40 crores, Q1 was about INR8 crores
items.quote: I think the capex outlook is going to be between INR35 crores to INR40 crores. This quarter, was about INR8 crores or so.

items.statement: Early signals of slowdown in U.S. construction equipment end market; Europe also witnessing softness in construction equipment end market
items.quote: There are some early signals of slowdown in U.S. construction equipment end market. Europe, as alluded earlier as well, is also witnessing softness in construction equipment end market.

items.statement: India domestic tractor market steady after previous fiscal softness; midterm expectations linked to monsoon 2024 and festive season demand
items.quote: India domestic tractor market is looking steady after the softness in previous fiscal year. Midterm expectations were now more linked to the monsoon 2024 performance and the festive season demand.

items.statement: New awards pipeline remains encouraging with added traction in all product verticals including PMP, large agricultural equipment assembly, agriculture machinery in India, high-horsepower 3PL, and geographical expansion in below 70-horsepowe
items.quote: New awards pipeline remains encouraging with added traction in all product verticals including PMP, large agricultural equipment assembly, agriculture machinery in India, high-horsepower 3PL as well as further geographical expansion in below 70-horsepower tractors.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 reported EBITDA margin at 17.6%; operating cash flow generation approximately INR50 crores
items.quote: Reported EBITDA for Q1 was INR46 crores, which is a quarter-on-quarter change of minus 10.6%, and year-on-year change of minus 23.6%, while reported EBITDA margin was at 17.6% for the quarter. Operating cash flow generation for the quarter was approximately INR50 crores.

items.statement: Inflationary pressure on operating costs remain in medium term to be partially mitigated through operating efficiencies
items.quote: Inflationary pressure on operating costs remain in the medium term to be partially mitigated through operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Macro concerns over global economic slowdown, geopolitical uncertainties and impact of worldwide high interest rates continue to remain a key monitorable
items.quote: Macro concerns over global economic slowdown, geopolitical uncertainties and impact of worldwide high interest rates continues to remain a key monitorable.

items.statement: Large ag segment (approx 20% of revenue) seeing 20-25% reduction due to end market decline of 10-12% plus inventory correction; construction equipment (37% of revenue) flat to low single digit down; small ag (30% of revenue) slightly better
items.quote: large ag that used to form about 18%, 20% of our business, that even though the market – end market is down by about 10% to 12%, we are seeing almost a 20%, 25% reduction. So the impact -- even though it's a small one, the impact over there is fairly large. In the small ag, it forms almost about 30% of our business, but it's – the inventory corrections are out, but the market is still slow. So we

items.statement: Long-term revenue growth expectation of 15-16% vs market growth of 5-6%, driven by new product platforms and market share gains
items.quote: No. I think our expectation on these two -- markets are going to be 5% to 6% growth go forward. We are looking at growth by longer term. This thing is to stay at about a 15% to 16% growth. So we expect to beat it by a significant larger number. But it won't be just by increased market share, it's by adding more products as well.

items.statement: Capacity utilization overall in range of 55% to 60% currently; not product-specific as factories produce both 3PL and PMP with common processes
items.quote: So to your first question, the capacity utilization overall is in the range of 55% to 60%, currently. It is not product-specific. Pretty much all our factories, except the U.S. one, which produces only PMP. All our India factories produce both 3PL and PMP.

items.statement: Interest rate cuts expected to drive recovery in small ag and small construction equipment; large ag recovery may take about a year due to low commodity prices and stretched farm income
items.quote: I don't see the serious farmer buying large equipment at least for about a year because this cycle will play through for the moment. But I do expect interest rates to kind of start showing up something on the small ag and the small construction equipment. And aftermarket has already come out in any case.

items.statement: Crude steel production target of 20.87 million tons and sales volume target of 19.26 million tons for FY25
items.value: 20.87 million tons crude steel; 19.26 million tons sales
items.quote: Volume target for this year, we are planning a crude steel production of around 20.87 million tons and sales volume of around about 19.26 million tons.

items.statement: FY25 capex projected at INR6,300 crores; similar range of INR7,000 crores for FY26; real jump from FY27 onwards
items.quote: For FY 2024-25, we have projected around about INR6,000 crores. It's actually INR6,300 crores, which we have given to the ministry. And the expenditure in the coming year also will be in the similar range around about INR7,000 crores or something. The real jump in the capex will come from, you can say, 2026-27 onwards.

items.statement: Debottlenecking to add 3 million tons capacity over 3-4 years with INR10,000-11,000 crores investment
items.quote: So we are planning to bring it up by 3 million tons in the next 3 to 4 years by putting in something like INR10,000 crores to INR11,000 crores of impact.

items.statement: IISCO 4 million ton greenfield expansion approved at Stage 1 with INR37,000 crores investment; tendering starting shortly
items.quote: One particular plant, IISCO plant, already the Board has accorded stage 1 approval for that. And it is that -- it's a 4 million ton plant, and the total investment will be around INR37,000 crores.

items.statement: Bokaro expansion to 7 million tons (+2.4 mt) and Durgapur to 3 million tons (+0.9 mt) under evaluation; consultant costs being reworked
items.quote: And the other 2 plants which are there, they are basically brownfield expansion in which Bokaro is going to be ramped up to 7 million tons. And Durgapur, we'll be going up by around about, you can say 1 million -- around 1 million tons.

items.statement: Hopeful of realization and margin improvement in coming quarters; cost reduction efforts ongoing via coal diversification and techno-economic parameters
items.quote: Going forward, the boost from the various measures being taken by the government on infrastructure spending orders well for the steel demand in the country with the overall outlook positive for the sustaine d growth in domestic consumption. We are hopeful of the realization and consequently the margin will improve for the company in the quarters to come

items.statement: Q1 blended NSR INR53,700/t; July decline INR500-600/t; August further decline INR1,000-1,500/t; Q2 NSR expected lower than Q1
items.quote: The NSR for Q1, it's in the range of INR53,700. Going forward, like we are -- it has declined further in the month of J uly by, you can say, around about INR500 to INR600. And there is a further reduction in the month of August also

items.statement: Long product NSR INR54,000/t, flat product NSR INR53,500/t in Q1; July drop INR700-800/t long, INR1,500/t flat; August drop ~INR1,000-1,500/t both
items.quote: In the long segment, the NSR was in the range of, you can say, around about INR54,000 crores. And in the flat, it was INR53,500 crores. Then the average was coming to around about INR53,700 crores.

items.statement: Imported coking coal landed cost INR24,500/t, indigenous INR13,500/t, blended ~INR23,000/t in Q1; expected similar in Q2 due to inventory consumption
items.quote: The imported coking coal was in the range of around about INR24,500 per ton landed at our steel plant and the indigenous was around INR13,500 per ton. So the average is working out to around about INR23,000 per ton.

items.statement: Q3 coking coal cost reduction expected if spot rates sustain; depends on August-September finalized rates
items.quote: Yes, Q3, there will be a reduction of around about you can say -- But then again, it depends on the supply or the rates which are being finalized in this August, September quarter -- in this August, September month.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand outlook positive driven by infrastructure investment; India projected >8% growth; long segment to benefit from infra spend, flats challenged by imports
items.quote: Going forward, the boost from the various measures being taken by the government on infrastructure spending orders well for the steel demand in the country with the overall outlook positive for the sustaine d growth in domestic consumption

items.statement: Semis share in production 15%, sales 7%; will remain at similar levels for ~3-3.5 years until new mills commission; then virtually zero
items.quote: The semis will remain at almost at the same levels. It will not come down drastically. The only thing is that our basic target is to maximize conversion through our conversion agents and wet leasing agents. So this we'll be doing it. But I don't see much of a reduction in the percentage of semis.

items.statement: Supreme Court judgment on state levies: Jharkhand INR100/t on iron ore/coal (~INR100-200 cr impact); Odisha clarity awaited; no major contingent liability currently
items.quote: and Madhya Pradesh. And i n case of Jharkhand, we have recently announced that they'll be imposing INR100 per ton -- per ton for iron ore and coal. Steel Authority of This is going to have a prospective effect of around INR150 crores to INR100 crores -- you can say, under INR200 crores

items.statement: Coke rate improved to 428 kg/thm in Q1 vs 440 kg FY24 average; target further 6-8 kg reduction in balance year; CDI rate to increase 10-12 kg
items.quote: This year we have targeted 440, but we may not be ab le to achieve that. We may not be here. But I'm sure that another you can say 6 to 8 kg of coal will be during the balance period

items.statement: Pellet plant at Gua mines 4 million tons in 3.5-4 years; COM basis pellet plant in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: We have our own plans of setting up a plant at Gua Ore Mines, a pellet plant at Gua Ore Mines of 4 million ton. So this should take around of 3.5 to 4 years from now.

items.statement: IISCO expansion IRR ~18% based on 3-year average steel prices and stamp charge battery cost savings; to be reworked before Stage 2
items.quote: It's IISCO plant and we have made an analysis. It's quite favorable. I think it's 18% -- 18% is IRR.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers revenue target ~Rs 200 crore in FY25 with ~40% EBIT margin and 20-25% annual growth
items.quote: Going by the 1st Quarter, we are very confident that we shall achieve ballpark Rs. 200 crore turnovers with EBITDA margins or EBIT margins in the region of about 40%. And we expect a 20%-25% growth rate year-on-year on this business.

items.statement: Film business value-added/specialty share target 40% by FY26 from 30% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Share of value-added and specialty products stood at 30% during the quarter and we are hoping to scale it up to 40% by FY26.

items.statement: Ester Filmtech revenue target Rs 450-500 crore at optimal utilization by FY26
items.quote: We expect the entity to generate revenues of a bout Rs. 450 to 500 crore upon achieving optimal utilization at reasonable prices /margins by next fiscal

items.statement: Loop JV capex $165 million funded 60-40 debt-equity; equity split 50-50 between Ester and Loop; minimal FY25 spend as groundbreaking in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, very simple, we have a CAPEX of about $165 million which is going to be funded at 60 - 40, outside could be 70-30. If we take 60-40, $66 million will be the equity which will be shared 50-50 between Ester and Loop and the balance about $100 million will be raised as debt in the joint venture company.

items.statement: Loop JV commercial production target first half of calendar 2027
items.quote: Our target timeline is to commence commercial production in the first half of calendar 2027.

items.statement: Domestic polyester film demand ~65,000 tons/month; exports ~20,000 tons/month; total demand ~85,000 tons vs effective capacity ~100,000 tons; gap narrowed to ~15,000 tons
items.quote: Domestic demand is estimated at about 65,000 tons per month a nd export is taking away about 20,000 tons. So, total demand for Film, domestic plus exports is about 85,000 tons against the effective operational capacity of 100,000 tons. The demand supply gap has now narrowed to about 15,000 tons

items.statement: Current BOPET spread Rs 37-38/kg vs Q1 FY25 average Rs 17-18/kg; June exit at Rs 26/kg; July at Rs 35-38/kg
items.quote: So, the spreads over PTA MEG would be in the region of about Rs. 37 to 38 per kilo as we speak now.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers Q1 FY25 EBIT margin 43% on Rs 45 crore revenue; 982 tons volume vs 526 tons YoY
items.quote: Q1 registered revenues of Rs. 45 crore with an impressive EBIT margin of 43% largely on the back of higher off -take of our marquee products, namely M B03 and Innovative PBT.

items.statement: Ester Industries value-added/specialty films 30% of volume (3,200 tons) and 42% of value in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Ester Industries, the total quantity of Films told was about 11,250 tons, out of which value-added and Specialty Film was close to 30%, 3200 tons. In terms of value quantity, it was 30%, but in terms of value, it was 42% of the sales made by the company.

items.statement: Value-added film spreads Rs 55-65 over base; export blended spreads Rs 65-75; commodity domestic spread Rs 17-18 in Q1
items.quote: As I have told you the differential will be around Rs. 55 to Rs. 65.

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization target 75-80% for FY25; Ester Filmtech volume 32,000-34,000 tons vs 25,600 tons FY24
items.quote: On a consolidated basis for year as a whole we are estimating our capacity utilization at 75% to 80% or a little better than that.

items.statement: Plastic Waste Management Rules effective April 1, 2025 mandate 10% recycled content in flexible packaging; expected to shift demand from BOPP to polyester
items.quote: Plastic waste management rules are scheduled to come into force from April 1, 2025. These rules will mandate utilization of 10% recycled content in flexible packaging laminate. This is expected to lead to increased demand and consequent better margins for Polyester Film with conversion taking place from other substrates like BOPP to Polyester.

items.statement: One BOPET line (3,500-3,700 tons) starting in next 2-3 months included in 110,000 tons capacity; another line in FY26; next after that in 2027
items.quote: is coming next year, how much would the capacity be approximately? Arvind Singhania: 3,500-3,700 tons. It is not going to make basic growth in demand. I don't think that is going to upset the apple cart

items.statement: Ester Filmtech Q1 FY25 positive EBITDA; revenue Rs 81 crore on 6,501 tons
items.quote: Better pricing environment resulted in positive EBITDA for the quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 overall company margin was about 13% and electrical cable segment margin slightly over 11%
items.quote: So, we closed the quarter with about 13% margin overall for the company and slightly over 11% for the electrical cable segment.

items.statement: Copper prices touched a high of $10,857 and low of $8,809 on LME in Q1 FY25, a difference of almost 20%
items.quote: Copper, for instance, touched a high of $10,857 on LME and also a low of $8,809 on the LME in the same quarter. So, that’s a difference o f almost 20

items.statement: Price cuts of about 10% were taken from June onwards in electrical wires due to copper price decline
items.quote: I think we took overall from then till now about 10%.

items.statement: Demand expected to pick up once copper prices stabilize around $8,800-$9,000 levels; festival season expected to boost auto demand
items.quote: I think demand will start to p ick up maybe once there is stability at the price level. If people see that the prices remain at 8,800, 9,000 levels, probably demand will pick up immediately afterwards

items.statement: Total CAPEX outflow for FY25 and FY26 around 500 crores, bulk spent in FY25; E-beam equipment installed awaiting AERB clearance, auto cable expansion at Roorkee by mid-Oct to mid-Nov, Goa compounding plant by May-Jun next year
items.quote: Overall expenditure until next year would still be around 500 crores. Bulk of it would be spent this year.

items.statement: EHV order book close to 300 crores; target revenue for FY25 is 240 crores
items.quote: We have a fairly decent order book there. Our current order book is close to 300 odd crores.

items.statement: FMEG business at 68 crores quarterly revenue, annualized ~272 crores, breakeven expected around 250 crores annual revenue
items.quote: 68 crores is what we have done in this quarter, times 4 is just over 250. And I think at this speed, we will be breaking even, barring any blips.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin range for consolidated entity (ex-dividends) is 13-13.5%
items.quote: But if you exclude that, 13%, 13.5% is something that you should work on.

items.statement: Optic fiber volumes up ~10% in Q1 FY25 but realizations lower due to global fiber price decline; fiber prices expected to recover over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: While optic fiber volumes were better by about 10%, although realizations were lower because of the ongoing low prices on fiber across the globe. We expect the fiber prices to recover over the next 2-3 quarters.

items.statement: OFC capacity expansion: preform plant (100 tons = 4M km fiber) operational by Dec/Jan, fiber draw towers from 4M to 6M km in 3-4 months then to 8M km; cabling capacity may expand from 8M to 10M km based on BharatNet outcome
items.quote: we are putting up a preform plant . So, we gain control over th e raw material that goes into the fiber . We are adding capacity on the fiber draw towers so that currently we have a 4 million draw capacity. We will take it up to 8 million over two stages

items.statement: Communication cable EBITDA margins targeting double digits (9-11%) over two steps; achievable by FY26-27 if volumes materialize
items.quote: Yes, if the numbers, if the volume comes in, then I don't see that as a major challenge.

items.statement: EHV execution challenges: ROW permissions, long L1-to-contract signing delays, utility funding constraints causing project delays
items.quote: You need to get ROW permissions , which are a problem in our count ry. While you may get it from the civic authorities, as you go to execute it, a lot of people start popping up from the ground that managing them is a challenge

items.statement: Agri cables demand strong in April-May but lean season now; next pickup expected around November pre-sowing season
items.quote: Agri was good both April and May. In fact, we were unable to keep up with the demand between April and May. Now is the lean season. So, the next pick up on agri would happen somewhere around November time frame.

items.statement: Targeting 150 to 175 branches and expansion to 12 states by adding Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh with 25 branches in southern states.
items.quote: As we speak, we have 113 branches, and we are on track to achieve 150 to 175 branches. Currently, we have presence in 8 states and soon in this quarter, we will expand our presence to 12 states.

items.statement: Secured loans share increased from 8% to 27% of AUM; targeting over 40% by end of 2025.
items.quote: Last year, it was only 8% of our AUM, which as on June stands at 27%. We will continue to increase contribution from secured loans, and it will be over 40% by end of 2025.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost reduced to 12.05%; expect further 50 bps reduction in H2 with equity infusion and credit rating upgrade.
items.quote: Incremental borrowing costs reduced to 12.05%. If you see that, you know, in H2 of last year, it was 13%, while our average borrowing rate is around 13.7%, but incrementally the decline is sharp. And with increasing capital base by end of this month, we believe further in H2 we should be able to bring down cost by another 50 basis points.

items.statement: Credit cost at 2.36% in Q1 vs 1.88% in Q4; guided blended credit cost to remain 2-3% (unsecured 2-3%, secured up to 1.5%).
items.quote: Historically, the company credit cost was less than 3%, including pandemic. And that's what we still maintain as we always say that on unsecured, we believe credit cost to remain between 2-3% and in secured portfolio maybe up to 1%, 1.5%, which will mean on a blended level, we should be around 2% of credit costs and not crossing that asset class portfolio increases.

items.statement: Targeting ROE of around 12% for FY25, up from 10% in FY24.
items.quote: We feel that ROE should reach which was about 10% in last year, we should see an elevation maybe somewhere around 12% is our idea that we should see.

items.statement: FY25 AUM guidance INR 1,300-1,400 crores; branch target 160-175; disbursement target INR 1,100 crores.
items.quote: FY25, as we guided, we in terms of AUM, we believe that anywhere between INR 1,300 crore and INR 1,400 crore, we should reach in terms of AUM. In terms of branches, the target is to have 175 branches, with the minimum number to be at 160.

items.statement: Leverage to be maintained below 4x on balance sheet; net worth expected to exceed INR 500 crores by mid next year to support INR 2,500 crores AUM in FY26.
items.quote: Largely, if you see that we are sorted, I'm definitely not saying that we will not raise equity next year. But with INR 175 crores of existing equity, INR 270 crores of infusion over the next 18 months, maybe a PAT of, say, minimum within next 1 year of INR 60 crores. I mean, in terms of going to next year as well, say, middle of next year, we'll have a net worth of INR 500 crores, which is enough

items.statement: Q1 muted due to seasonality (30% of yearly disbursement in H1); expect pickup in H2 with branch expansion, monsoon improvement, and festival season.
items.quote: H2 will see the pickup because there -- so what are the levers are that branches which we are developing. In Q2, you will see very significant number of branches which will come up in South and even other regions. We already have 13 new branches. There's a very large number which is now coming. Our team is hired in South, so that will play some role in H2.

items.statement: Maintaining spread of at least 15% over medium to long term; Q1 incremental spread improved 49 bps despite secured loan growth.
items.quote: What we have always maintained that we will have a spread of at least over 15% over a medium to long term perspective because this model has its own, you know, OpEx. So that will be maintained. However, if you see, we believe that given the decline in borrowing costs, we should not see any deterioration in spreads.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded by CRISIL from BBB- to BBB Stable; expect another upgrade within calendar year driven by AUM growth, secured lending, improving ROA, and equity capital.
items.quote: The other thing which happened in this quarter is improvement in our credit rating by CRISIL from BBB minus to BBB stable, which will now we expect that in another 5-6 months' time, maybe within this calendar year, we should see one more upgrade, especially driven by increasing AUM, increasing secure lending, improving ROA and most importantly equity capital.

items.statement: Collection efficiency for June at 95.5%; introduced collection incentives and legal recovery processes to manage asset quality.
items.quote: And the collection efficiency for the month of June is above 95%. It's about 95.5%.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth expected at 12% to 15%
items.quote: So this year we should be somewhere around 2 digits, somewhere between 12% to 15%, something of that nature.

items.statement: Full year revenue growth of 12% to 14% expected
items.quote: But for the whole year, we would still expect that 12% to 14% kind of growth on the whole year basis to come through?

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected at 33-34% for now
items.quote: I think 33%, 34% is what probably one should look at it now as of now.

items.statement: R&D center at Nashik to be operational after June next year
items.quote: No, we haven't shared. But as of now, like we feel in the -- after the June of next year, it should be in a working condition.

items.statement: Serra business expected flat to 5% growth; growth to come from other segments
items.quote: So if you talk about Serra business we don't expect a lot of growth to come. It should be a more or less flat business or maybe like 5% here and there.

items.statement: Anti-inflammatory enzyme sales declined 20% YoY to INR280 million in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The sale of our largest product, which is anti-inflammatory enzyme, stood at INR280 million for the first quarter of FY '25 as compared to INR352 million in Q1 of FY '24, so there's a de-growth of about 20%.

items.statement: India business under pressure this year, growth expected in second half
items.quote: India business is supposed to be under pressure this year, particularly on the human side. Most of the growth is supposed to come into the second half of this year.

items.statement: European market slowed down; US market showing growth
items.quote: European is a little bit slowed dow n as of now. That is what we can see. In terms of U.S., probably we are growing into these areas, because our sale was very low on the consumption

items.statement: Freight cost up INR5 million YoY; partial pass-through to customers
items.quote: Yes some burden is there. If I compare on year-on-year basis, probably the freight cost is up by about INR5 million.

items.statement: Evoxx has one big order under negotiation worth EUR 1.4-1.5 million for one year
items.quote: It will be not very big, but it will be about EUR 1.4 million to EUR 1.5 million.

items.statement: No current legal conflicts or expected settlements
items.quote: No. As of today, there is no conflict. But you never know.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 60-65%; 1% revenue increase drives 2-3x EBITDA increase
items.quote: So current capacity utilization is around 60% to 65%.

items.statement: Wellfa brand expected INR2-3 crores sales this year
items.quote: we feel that this year, we should be having about INR2 crores to INR3 crores sales coming from the Welllfa brand.

items.statement: Target INR1,000 crores revenue in 4-5 years
items.quote: in down the line 4 to 5 years, we target to achieve INR1,000 crores of revenue.

items.statement: R&D spend expected at 6% consolidated including capex; INR50 crores spent on Nashik center so far
items.quote: when you really prepare a sort of model, you can look at about 6% as our total R&D spend on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance raised to Rs. 15,000-16,000 crores for FY25 from earlier Rs. 10,000-12,000 crores
items.quote: we are confident that we will get an order inflow of Rs. 15,000 crores to 16,000 crores for the full year.

items.statement: Revenue expected to decline 5% in FY25 versus earlier flat guidance
items.quote: we would actually be looking at a 5% degrowth from last year's number.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance revised to 11-12% for FY25 from earlier 11-13%
items.quote: I would say 11%, 12% is a good figure to kind of think about given the, like I said, some of the challenges around the depleting order book.

items.statement: Target net debt of Rs. 1,000 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: we will achieve our target debt levels of Rs. 1,000 crores net debt by the end of this fiscal year, as we had indicated on our last call.

items.statement: Aim to become net cash company by FY26
items.quote: Yes, that is the agenda, sir.

items.statement: Standalone CAPEX guidance of Rs. 150-170 crores for FY25
items.quote: FY '25 we can guide you now, because the total CAPEX would be in the range of Rs. 150 crores to Rs. 170 crores.

items.statement: Order book updated to Rs. 18,600 crores including Rs. 2,400 crores from coal MDOs
items.quote: in our current order of Rs. 18,600 crores, we have added three years coal MDOs of Rs. 2,400 crores.

items.statement: Ordering activity weak in Q1 due to elections but expected to pick up in H2
items.quote: During the quarter under review, ordering activity was weak across all sectors, which was as expected because of the elections, but now is expected to pick up.

items.statement: Target order book mix of two-thirds EPC and one-third HAM/BOT
items.quote: two-thirds of the order book would be straight up EPC, one-third would be HAM/BOT, like any kind of PPP project.

items.statement: Payment delays from JJM projects increased debtors and working capital temporarily
items.quote: We have experienced payment related challenges primarily from JJM projects that resulted in higher debtors and stretched working capital.

items.statement: Alpha InvIT stake sale proceeds of Rs. 478 crores; Rs. 190 crores received in July, balance in Q2/Q3
items.quote: out of this Rs. 478 crores which is shown in page number 26 of our Investor Presentation, around Rs. 190 crores precisely we received in July

items.statement: Pachhwara MDO produced 1.46 MT in Q1, on track for 7 MT full year capacity
items.quote: Here, we are on target to achieve the 7 million metric tonnes which is the full capacity for this.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of less than Rs. 25,000 crores at current juncture
items.quote: I think less than Rs. 25,000 crores where we have already bid out.

items.statement: Optic fiber bids submitted for 16 packages worth Rs. 50,000+ crores in JV with Sterlite
items.quote: there were 16 packages and in total about Rs. 50,000 crores plus of order book for us.

items.statement: Finance cost expected at Rs. 350-400 crores for FY25 despite Q1 debt increase
items.quote: we still believe the debt cost will be between Rs. 350 crores to Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Management reiterates 20%-25% growth guidance for both topline and EBITDA
items.quote: I think our guidance would remain the same actually looking at the 20% -25% growth, both in EBITDA and in topline.

items.statement: Non-steel segment EBITDA margin improved to 6.5% with gross margin at 10%-12%
items.quote: With improving economies in the non -steel segment, our EBITDA margin for the segment has improved to 6.5%.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin expanded 15 basis points to 3.2% with 20% EBITDA growth
items.quote: Our steadfast commitment to growing value-added segments for profitable growth, in line with our vision, led to a 20% year -on-year increase in our EBITDA, with a 15 basis point improvement in our EBITDA margins, to 3.2%.

items.statement: Plan to open 10 new fulfillment centers in next 6-9 months, targeting 135-136 total by year-end
items.quote: We have also identified 10 new strategic locations to set up new fulfillment centers over the next 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Retail footfall down due to elections and monsoons but inquiry pipeline encouraging for coming quarters
items.quote: Our retail footfall was, however, down this quarter in the backdrop of slow construction activity amid election and monsoons. Nevertheless, our inquiry pipeline is encouraging, and we expect a positive trajectory in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Finance costs increased significantly due to higher acceptances (Rs. 500 cr) at 9.25%-9.5% interest, may persist 1-2 quarters
items.quote: However, due to an increa se in our acceptances during this quarter, our finance cost has increased significantly, resulting in a profit after tax at Rs. 16 crores.

items.statement: Non-steel revenue target of Rs. 1,000+ crores (25%-30% of total) in 2-3 years
items.quote: Ideally, we are looking at non-steel revenues to be around 25%-30% of our total revenue. So, if we continue that in two to three years we are looking at non -steel revenues growing over Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Steel volumes grew 20% YoY to 177 kilo tonnes; flat products up 44% YoY; non-steel revenue up 35% YoY
items.quote: Our steel vertical continued to generate steady growth in revenues and volumes, steel volumes reaching 177-kilo tonnes this quarter, a 20% year-on-year increase

items.statement: Demerger of building materials marketplace business approved by SEBI, NCLT filing expected soon, implementation by Q4 FY25
items.quote: The demerger scheme has received approval from SEBI, and we have begun filing with NCLT. We expect the scheme to be implemented by Q4 FY 2025.

items.statement: Interest cost on acceptances at 9.25%-9.5%; total debt Rs. 620 cr including acceptances (Rs. 100 cr ex-acceptances)
items.quote: Approximately around 9.25% to 9.5%.

items.statement: Interest costs expected to remain elevated for 1-2 more quarters before normalizing
items.quote: One more quarter, we may continue the same thing.

items.statement: Manufacturing business targeting 5%-6% ROE post-demerger, improvement expected over 2-3 years
items.quote: We are looking around 5% to 6% ROE.

items.statement: Double-digit operating revenue growth targeted for FY25
items.quote: Firstly, we are looking to grow Operating revenues in double digits for the year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance upgraded to 17%-19% for FY25
items.quote: Thirdly, we have upgraded our EBITDA margin band guidance to 17%-19% (vs. 16%-18% guidance Last year) on account of higher Gross Margins.

items.statement: Expect to be net debt free for three quarters in FY25
items.quote: Finally, we look forward to continuing our Lazer sharp focus on working capital metrics and cash flows to continue. We will be Net Debt Free for 3 quarters during the year.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to be higher in FY25
items.quote: Secondly, we expect Gross margins to be higher during the year.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross margin at 72%, highest ever
items.quote: We had the highest ever gross margins in the company's history at 72% vs 69% last year.

items.statement: Average book price increase of 6%-8% for FY25
items.quote: But overall, the price increase is around, I would say depending on book to book, but an average increase would be 6% to 8% price increase this year.

items.statement: Expect 40%-50% of schools to adopt new curriculum in FY25 if books released on time
items.quote: But this year if the books come out on t ime, obviously depends on the timing also, if the books come out on time it will be 40 -50% this year who will adopt the new curriculum

items.statement: NCERT books for most classes expected by end of December (Q3 FY25)
items.quote: The discussions that we ha ve been having is that the books should be out by end of Q3, so that for the next academic year all the books are available so that there is no confusion in adoption by schools next year in the complete curriculum

items.statement: Content licensing for Gen AI LLMs opened new revenue vertical with 75%-80% margins
items.quote: Plus, apart from that, we are also doing some other projects, where we are also providing other content. So, I think this will be an ongoing business that we are trying to develop and it's pretty decent high -margin business, almost 75 to 80% margin in this.

items.statement: Paper procurement to be 25%-30% lower in FY25 due to leftover inventory
items.quote: We will be buying around 25 to 30% less paper than we buy in a normal year.

items.statement: Delayed NCERT book release beyond December could push adoption benefits to FY26
items.quote: If the books are released late then the sales and the adoption of the new curriculum books will be next year If the new books are launched before December, then we would see approx. 40% to 50% of schools adopting the new curriculum this year itself. If the books are released later, then that number might drop also.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 net working capital days at historic low of 132 days
items.quote: Our Q1 Net Working capital days was at 132 days which is the lowest in company's history.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 receivable days at historic low of 92 days
items.quote: In terms of receivable days, it stood at 92 days (vs. 103 days in Q1FY24), a reduction of 11 days over the previous year. This is the lowest receivable days in Q1 in in the company's history.

items.statement: Net cash balance increased to Rs882m at end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: We ended the quarter with a strong Net cash balance of Rs882m (Vs. Q4FY24: Rs600m).

items.statement: No incremental employee cost for content development beyond March 2025
items.quote: I would say that by the end of this year, most of it would be finished. So, we don't see incremental employee cost on the content development side beyond March 25.

items.statement: Sales return trend at 14%-15% for current season, lower than last year
items.quote: Yeah, the trend is lower than last year, so it's around 14%-15%.

items.statement: Total order book stands at INR646 crores including unexecuted order book of INR303 crores approximately
items.quote: As of now, the company's total order book stands at INR646 crores including unexecuted order book of INR303 crores approximately, indicating a strong pipeline and promising future.

items.statement: Order book expected to double to INR600 crores by end of FY25 from current INR300 crores plus unexecuted
items.quote: Order book, as I explained in previous discussion, order book is expected to be double. Today, it is INR300 crores plus. It is expected to be double by end of current financial year

items.statement: Expecting EBITDA margin of 20% plus for FY25, up from 17% plus in FY24
items.quote: Now this year, we are expecting 20% plus.

items.statement: Targeting 20% to 25% EBITDA margin with international projects not bid below 35% EBIT
items.quote: So EBIT, we are eying at 20% to 25%. Current year, definitely 20% plus.

items.statement: Strategically shifting focus from domestic to international markets for FY25 and FY26 targeting large-scale projects above INR50 crores
items.quote: Looking ahead, Dhruv is strategically shifting its focus from the domestic market to international markets for financial year '25 and '26. The company aims to target large-scale projects above INR50 crores

items.statement: Expecting order book to reach INR700 crores by end of FY25 from current INR300 crores plus
items.quote: So in short, my order book of INR300 crores should reach to INR700 crores by end of the financial year.

items.statement: 90% of order book to be executed in 2-3 years with construction period of 36 months
items.quote: So a straight answer to the question is, order book shall be executed -- 90% of the order book shall be executed in a period of 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: International market uncertainties include political volatility in 15-20 target countries and slow evaluation processes for World Bank aided projects
items.quote: Because all of sudden, uncertainties happen in international market, and we can't imagine that. Because we have put our bids to 15 to 20 countries, not 1 country. Few of them are politically volatile.

items.statement: Raised INR33 crores plus funds to buy extraordinary equipment for higher technical scores
items.quote: Since we are now successful in raising INR33 crores plus funds. Only exchange's approvals in principle are awaited, but investors are ready to deposit the money once the formalities are completed. So with that money, I'm going to buy some extraordinary equipment

items.statement: International projects expected to contribute INR50-100 crores to additional INR300 crores order book by FY25 end
items.quote: Additional INR300 crores, I can expect only INR50 crores to INR100 crores from international markets, even less than that.

items.statement: Expecting at least 2 international orders from World Bank and African Development Bank funded projects
items.quote: Definitely, at least 2.

items.statement: International consultancy fees start at 5% of project cost vs 2-3% in India, with EBIT not bid below 35%
items.quote: Here we are getting 2% to 3% as a consultancy fee of the project cost. And in Middle East, the fee starts itself from 5%.

items.statement: Payment cycles: NHAI 45-60 days, MoRTH 90-120 days, other clients 60-90 days, average 60-75 days for supervision work
items.quote: So average receipt of the supervision work is 60 to 75 days, which is 100% guaranteed, because we only work with the clients where there is a sufficient fund provision

items.statement: Successfully raised INR33 crores plus funds, exchange approvals in principle awaited
items.quote: Since we are now successful in raising INR33 crores plus funds. Only exchange's approvals in principle are awaited, but investors are ready to deposit the money once the formalities are completed.

items.statement: PAT margin target of 3-3.5% for FY25

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 6,300 crores by FY27 (INR 5,000 crores parent + INR 1,300 crores subsidiaries)
items.quote: For Sky Gold we have already given INR5,000 crores revenue to 2027 March and for the subsidiary is INR1,300 crores. So consolidated will be INR6,300 crores.

items.quote: To support our growth ambitions, we have planned a fundraiser of INR270 crores, which will be utilized across the multiple parameters, and will help the company to achieve the goal of INR6,300 crores by FY27.

items.statement: Ordering cycle of 30-45 days for corporate clients
items.quote: Already we have ordering cycle of 30-45 days. Basically, these are very confidential. We can't give much on this. But we have a cycle of 30-45 days.

items.statement: Gross margin target of 7-8% structurally through product mix and exports
items.quote: The gross margin stood at 6.4%. The quarterly volatility in gross margins is due to product mix changes. Structurally, we would like to reach 7-8% gross margin through product mix and exports.

items.statement: GML adoption to improve PAT margin by 0.5%
items.quote: GML will help us to reduce 0.5% of the sales, which 0.5% PAT will improve because of the GML. So that will help us to improve 0.5%.

items.quote: No, no, it's extraordinary growth we are seeing because right where we were in the exhibition from 9th August, I just skipped today. Today also exhibition is going on. So I think historic buying is there in the total historic booking is there.

items.statement: Diamond jewellery sales to reach 10-15% of turnover in four quarters
items.quote: In four quarters, diamond jewellery sales will come to 10% to 15% of our turnover. That will help us to improve our margin, yes.

items.statement: 18-carat market share growing from 3% to 5% of production
items.quote: Last year, we produced 97% of 22-carat and 3% of 18-carat. Now, the market is expanding for 18-carat also. In India, 22-carat market was 99%. Now, it is 95%. 5% 18-carat market also has grown.

items.statement: Capacity of 750 kg/month parent + 300 kg/month subsidiaries = 1,050 kg/month total
items.quote: Already in parent company I told we have put in the PPT also that we have 750 kg per month capacity and subsidiaries both together we have 300 kg per month capacity. So both together can go up to 1050 kg per month and yearly 12 ton we can produce.

items.quote: This year, we are targeting to keep up to 350-360 kgs per month we will produce in this year.

items.statement: Export contribution guidance of 9-10% for FY25
items.quote: Sir, we have already given the guidance in the last quarter that in this year we will go up to 9%-10% from the exports. So, we will sustain this growth up to 9%-10%. This quarter is 11%, but 10% is sustainable for this year.

items.statement: 100% GML utilization by December quarter
items.quote: Already this quarter, we have shifted that we were using 10% of GML. This quarter, we will be using approximately 30% of GML. And December quarter, 100% we will be using GML.

items.statement: Inventory fully hedged on MCX, no impact from gold price fluctuations
items.quote: Nothing, because our inventory is totally hedged in the MCX. So, we don't have any impact of any rise or fall also on the inventory.

items.statement: Subsidiaries Star Mangalsutra and Sparkling Chains to scale to INR 1,200-1,300 crores in two years
items.quote: So, we have both have capacity to go up to INR1,200 crores and INR1,300 crores in two years. Already last year we did INR370 crores sorry, last year. And this year we can make it INR600 crores to INR700 crores from both the entities.

items.statement: Standalone revenue target of Rs. 900-1,000 crore by FY26 with organic at Rs. 700-750 crore, BuLi at ~Rs. 100 crore, inorganic at ~Rs. 150 crore
items.quote: I would say Rs. 700 crore to Rs. 750 crore for organic, around Rs. 100-odd crore for BuLi and another about Rs. 150-odd crore for inorganic.

items.statement: Battery chemicals brownfield capacity to contribute Rs. 200-250 crore in FY26 with Greenfield adding more in H2 FY26
items.quote: The capacity which are coming online in the Brownfield in Dahej in this year itself can contribute around Rs. 200 crore to Rs. 250 crore.

items.statement: Full utilization of 30 KTA electrolyte capacity targeted by FY28-FY29
items.quote: So, we feel confident that our target to reach full utilization level by FY28 or FY29. That continues to remain, and we are on track to do that.

items.statement: Financial closure achieved for bulk of Greenfield battery chemicals CAPEX with favourable terms; construction commenced
items.quote: I am glad to share that we have achieved financial closure for bulk of the CAPEX with favourable terms. Construction work has already commenced and we remain on track for strategically commissioning this facility in FY26

items.statement: SBI term loan of Rs. 9 billion for Pakhajan Greenfield site with 2-year moratorium, 10-year repayment, graduated installments
items.quote: Basically we received from SBI for especially our Pakhajan Greenfield site, we have already received the funding and it has a two year moratorium and it has a 10 year repayment

items.statement: Additional Rs. 2.5 billion funding tied up with existing bankers for Dahej expansion; Rs. 1 billion secured, Rs. 1.5 billion under discussion
items.quote: Out of Rs. 2.5 billion we have already secured around Rs. 1 billion and another Rs. 1.5 billion is under discussion.

items.statement: BuLi Chem Q2 order book very strong, expecting full capacity utilization; in-principle environmental clearance received for 2x capacity debottlenecking
items.quote: In fact, Q1 was better than earlier and in Q2 also we are seeing a very good order book where we feel we will be fully utilizing its capacity.

items.statement: Targeting 16-17% EBITDA margins for lithium salts business; ROCE target of 20%
items.quote: In the past also we have said that we expect like ROCE of 20% and also we are targetting, depending on price of lithium somewhere around 16% to 17% kind of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Lithium raw material prices stabilized in $11.5 +/- $1.5 range for last 1-2 quarters; organic chemical prices also seen bottom
items.quote: we saw raw material prices hit their bottom and now they generally trade in a narrow band of around $10 - $12 or $13, so let us say $11.5 +/- $1.5 for last one or two quarters.

items.statement: Strong demand for non-Chinese lithium salts/electrolytes from derisking; MoUs and pricing commitments initiated with international customers
items.quote: We continue to see strong demand for non-Chinese supply of lithium salts and electrolytes from derisking standpoint and have accordingly initiated discussions through MoUs, pricing commitments with international customers.

items.statement: Expect to sign long-term electrolyte contracts with 2-3 major Indian battery makers (Ola, Exide, Amara Raja) within next 18 months
items.quote: So, in the next 18 months, we should be able to convince two out of three or three out of three customers to basically sign up with Neogen and get into long-term agreement for electrolytes.

items.statement: Semiconductor opportunity emerging with three engines: organolithium compounds, 99.99%+ purity specialty gases, high-purity organic chemicals; few crore to few tens of crore in FY25
items.quote: It will be a few crore getting into a few tens of crore in the current financial year. We are just starting with that and then we will see how we can ramp it up.

items.statement: Customs duty exemption on lithium carbonate/hydroxide reduces local raw material cost, making electrolyte more competitive domestically
items.quote: lithium carbonate and lithium hydroxide. Abhijit Akella: So, it is a straight saving in our raw material cost? Dr. Harin Kanani: Yes, yes. So, in the international market, it does not make so much of a difference because anyway we would have advance licence because ultimately it is getting exported. But when we are selling it locally to that extent our cost goes down

items.statement: Japan subsidiary incorporated with senior hire to accelerate battery materials, CSM and n-butyl lithium business development in Japan/Korea
items.quote: We are very fortunate that we are able to hire a very senior level person who has many years of experience leading a Japanese agrochemical company in Japan as well as in India. So, he is helping us with all our strategy and our business development activities.

items.statement: Organic capacity sufficient until Rs. 1,000 crore standalone revenue; no significant organic CAPEX planned for FY25-FY26, focus on debottlenecking and mix optimization
items.quote: On the organic side, we have capacity, till Neogen reaches around Rs. 1,000 crore. Neogen standalone, which is about Rs. 1,000 crore in which organic contribution would be somewhere around Rs. 700 to Rs. 750 crore. So, we already have capacity in place for that.

items.statement: Bathware aims to grow 1.25-1.5x market; market expected 8-10% in H2, full year mid-single digits
items.quote: We maintained our guidance around 1.25 to 1.5x the market. We've always maintained that for a long-term basis.

items.statement: Pipes volume growth guided at 16-18% for FY25
items.quote: But definitely, this complete year we will be growing by around 16% to 18% in volumes.

items.statement: Pipes targets double-digit EBITDA margin for full year FY25

items.statement: Total capex for Roorkee plant and debottlenecking INR170-180 crore in FY25; 40% spent, balance in next 9 months
items.quote: We feel that other than the pipe plant in Roorkee, which is coming up, which should be there working in this financial year total cost of around INR170 crore-INR180 crore, the normal capex should be ranging between INR70 crore to INR80 crore.

items.statement: Roorkee facility construction on track, commercial operations expected by Q3 FY25
items.quote: The construction of our Roorkee facility is progressing as planned, with commercial operations expected to commence by Q3FY25.

items.statement: Bathware Q1 EBITDA margin 12.9% (INR42 cr on INR326 cr); margin drop due to lower revenue, fixed cost absorption

items.statement: Consumer Appliances Q1 EBITDA margin 2.7% (INR3 cr on INR111 cr); improved via cost optimization and exiting furniture retail
items.quote: Our consumer Appliances business delivered INR111 crore in revenue with an EBITDA of INR3 crore at a 2.7% EBITDA margin reflecting the positive impact of cost optimization and exiting our loss-making retail furniture business.

items.statement: Pipes Q1 EBITDA margin 6.7% (INR11 cr on INR163 cr); flat YoY, expects improvement in H2

items.statement: Sales force consolidation expected to add 100+ bps to Bathware EBITDA margin annually
items.quote: We believe that it is going to help us increase our margins by 100 basis points plus on an annual basis.

items.statement: Brass prices cooled from INR600/kg to INR525-530/kg; outlook stable INR500-545/kg; no price hike needed

But we have seen cooling off of the brass prices now, which is down to INR525, INR530 range.

items.statement: PVC resin prices rose INR15/kg in May-June, then fell INR11/kg in July; trend downward, may bottom in 2 months
items.quote: In May and June, we had an upward trend, and the prices went up by around INR15 a kg. And we saw a good June contributing to the business. items.statement: Secondary sales improved late June and July; expect momentum through festive season and H2 recovery
items.quote: Early market inputs suggest secondary sales have seen noticeable upticks since late June and we anticipate further momentum building up through the festive season.

items.statement: Bathware economy/premium mix shifted to 52/48 in Q1 FY25 from 47/53 in Q1 FY24
items.quote: In Q1FY25, it was 52% for economy and 48% for premium. In Q1FY24, it was 47% for economy, and 53% for premium for us.

items.statement: Working capital pressure from inventory buildup; net debt up INR100 cr QoQ; target to reduce working capital days by 10-15 by year-end
items.quote: We believe that we can easily bring it down by about 10 to 15 days by the end of the year.

items.statement: Core revenue growth guidance of 14% to 18% for FY25, excluding compost and RDF sales
items.quote: We would be talking around 14% to 18% of growth on core revenues, and this excludes sale of compost, RDF because those are something that we will expect a sharp change in the second half of the year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 23% to 24% for FY25
items.quote: And EBITDA margins to be around the levels that we have for Q1, which is around 23% to 24%. That is our planned internal hurdle rate.

items.statement: Capex for vehicle scrapping and tire recycling projects estimated at Rs.20 crores to Rs.28 crores plus incremental Rs.8 crores to scale up
items.quote: The investment will be in line with what we have announced. It would be around Rs.20 crores to Rs.28 crores for both the projects and maybe an incremental Rs.8 crores to scale up the entity.

items.statement: One large C&T contract likely to close in Q2 FY25
items.quote: One of the projects is likely to close in this quarter, at least one large C&T contract is likely to close.

items.quote: Over the last 2 quarters, we have demonstrated steady improvement in the reported margin, which now stands at 23.8%. And we believe this range of 23% to 24% will serve as a base going forward.

items.statement: Expect RDF sales growth momentum to continue
items.quote: We expect this growth momentum in RDF sales to continue.

items.statement: Vehicle scrapping and tire recycling projects expected EBITDA margin of 8% to 12%

items.quote: down the line, if you ask me, for FY 26, FY 27, definitely we are expecting high teen to 20% growth, year on year.

items.quote: Again, more or less not significant. Again, it would be in the range of 40 to 50 crores.

items.quote: For the today, I can say that we are at around 50% originator, 50% generic in pharma, whereas 80%, 20% in pharma and commodity. On the future, I can't disclose exact number, but that definitely originator business will be higher beyond above 50%.

items.statement: Board approved new capex up to INR1,300 crores for 35,000 MT per annum OTR radial tire capacity at Bhuj, to be executed in phases
items.quote: Accordingly, we are embarking on a new capex spend of up to INR1,300 crores for 35,000 metric ton per annum at Bhuj. This will be executed in various phases.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex guidance between INR600-700 crores, Q1 spend was INR200 crores
items.quote: Full year would be between INR600 crores to INR700 crores.

items.statement: Advanced carbon black project of 30,000 MT progressing well, on schedule for commissioning in H1 FY25
items.quote: We are working on advanced carbon black project with a capacity of 30,000 metric tons. This project is progressing well and is as per schedule.

items.statement: Management striving for full year FY25 EBITDA margin around 24.8% (last year's level) despite Q1 at 26.04% and expected cost pressures
items.quote: Last year, full year, our EBITDA margin was around 24.8%, and we will be striving for the same range for the whole of the year.

items.statement: Raw material costs expected to increase 2-3% in coming quarters, freight costs to rise to 8-9% of revenue in Q2 from 6.4% in Q1
items.quote: Commodity prices are also going up. So raw material, approximately 2% to 3%, will increase the raw material cost.

items.statement: Demand slowing down across both agri and OTR segments in Europe and US due to recession fears, geopolitical issues; channel inventory increasing, OEM demand softer
items.quote: So, we are yet seeing a market weaknesses come in this, also there are geopolitical scenarios with the backdrop of everything that's happening across various regions of Europe and Middle East, and also U.S. recession fears are there. items.statement: Retail volumes weak, channel inventory buildup occurred in Q1; Red Sea transit delays contributed to distributor stocking
items.quote: No, we are seeing it to be weak. That is why the channel buildup that I mentioned earlier has taken place.

items.statement: India market outlook remains positive, targeting expansion; India agri market share estimated 6-7%
