We are forming a separate landmark shared services vertical housed under one of our subsidiaries where all our employees of our call centre, insurance, HR, accounts, dri vers etc. will be housed and would work in a brand agnostic way

items.statement: Existing outlet EBITDA margin close to 18%; consolidated EBITDA margin at 16.5% for Q1 due to new outlet drag, expected to normalize as new outlets ramp up.
items.quote: What we have declared is a console thing that we have combined both sales and service over here. So it would be close to around 18% for existing brands. I can say that.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment improving from August; early indicators show upward trend in enquiries, test drives, footfalls; OEMs introducing offers; festive season outlook promising.
items.quote: Early indicators from August are quite encouraging. The customer enquiries, test drives and footfalls are showing an upward trend. OEMs have also started introducing customer offers which will help drive this momentum. We are expecting this to continue for the remainder of the year.

items.statement: Mahindra Thar Roxx launch on Aug 15; cars at dealerships first week of September; preponing Hyderabad outlet launch to capitalize.
items.quote: Though there is going to be a launch, the cars at the dealership are going to be available in the first week of September. So this is what we are closely in touch with the company and we are hoping to get this operationalized in the beginning of September at least one outlet where we can get this done.

items.statement: Inventory reduced to 41 days vs industry 67 days; comfort zone 30-35 days; will try to reduce further 5-7 days.
items.quote: So Raj, the inventory of new cars at the beginning was we were at around 41 days and which is still outside of our comfort zone. So we are happier with around 30 , 35 days of inventory. When let the world be at 60 days, 65 days, we don't want to carry that much invento ry. So we will still try to reduce it by 5, 7 days if we are able to do it

items.statement: Mercedes-Benz India guided for double-digit growth this year; E-Class launch in last quarter of calendar year; strong interest seen.
items.quote: Santosh Iyer has guided for a double digit growth for the year. That was the last interview of his that I saw. The E-class is getting launched in the last quarter of this calendar year. So we will see some numbers kicking in for us in the next quarter for E-class. Obviously, it is something that eagerly people are awaiting and we are seeing a great amount of interest.

items.statement: Mahindra announced capex of INR 26,000 crores over next three years; Landmark ramping up Kolkata operations, Hyderabad outlets operational soon.
items.quote: They have an exciting model pipeline and an announced capex of further INR26,000 crores over the next three years. Our operations in Kolkata are ramping up and the outlets in Hyderabad will be operational soon.

items.statement: Pre-owned car business revenue INR 27 crores in Q1, 69% YoY growth; confident of surpassing last year's performance.
items.quote: The pre -owned car business has been performing well with a revenue of INR27 crores in the quarter and 69% yea r-on-year growth. We are confident of surpassing last year's

items.statement: New e-commerce website launched; organic new users up 36%, user engagement up 65% in under a month.
items.quote: In a period of less than a month, we have seen an organic increase in new users by 36% and user engagement by over 65%.

items.statement: Expect good improvement from Q3 FY25 as new model launches (MG Windsor, BYD Atto-3, Mahindra vehicles, Mercedes E-Class) kick in.
items.quote: I would say that from Q3 for sure there will be good improvement. Even in these brands that we are talking about we will have new cars that are getting launched for which we had all been waiting and that should turn things around.

items.statement: Current order book is approximately INR400 crores with a strategic focus on completing projects within two to three years.
items.quote: The current order book of the company is approximately about INR400 crores, and with a strategic focus on completing this project within a span of two to three years.

items.statement: Optimistic about securing high-backed orders in the future with potential value of E-order ranging from INR300 to INR350 crores.
items.quote: We are very optimistic about securing high-backed orders in the future with the potential value of E-order to range from about INR300 to INR350 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 anticipating good growth compared to previous year; numbers not to be disclosed.
items.quote: So Q2 FY, we are anticipating good growth as compared to previous year. The numbers not to be disclosed, but you can expect a good growth compared to the previous quarters or previous year.

items.statement: Expecting margins to grow based on past trends of Q4 FY24 and Q1 FY25.
items.quote: Madam, we are expecting the same to grow as you can see from the past trends of Q4 of FY '23-'24, Q1 of '24-'25. So, you can see that it is improving better as compared to what we were doing previously.

items.statement: Government focus on electrical infrastructure expansion with central budget of INR2.5 lakh crores and similar state budgets, totaling ~INR4.5 lakh crores of tendering.
items.quote: So, which means we are looking at about INR4.5 lakh crores of tendering to be done. So, which means that if you look at it, which means if you look at it from my perspective, there are enough tenders going to come in and there are going to be lesser players to cater to this requirement.

items.statement: Planning to enter transmission segment (132 KV and above) post-October-November 2024 with tenders from state and central governments.
items.quote: Yes, the update portion is that post-November, I mean October-November, there is going to be a lot of tenders for the transmission sector to be coming in, where the tenders have already been finalized by the state and the central government.

items.statement: No significant capex plans for FY25; capex is in form of bank guarantees, performance guarantees, EMD, and PBG for bidding new tenders.
items.quote: Madam as expected there is no capex. The capex is in a form of bidding of the new tenders and the submission of the performance guarantee and mobilization of sites which is on a working capital purpose.

items.statement: Funds raised majorly for working capital and for acquisition of stake from 15% to 60% in Peaton Electrical Company Limited.
items.quote: So the fund has been raised for the purpose of the majorly for working capital purpose and for certain portion we are for the acquisition of a stake from 15% to 60% in our Peaton Electrical Company Limited.

items.statement: New product compact busway systems to be launched by December 2024 under Peaton Electrical; revenues expected in FY26.
items.quote: So, you will see those revenues coming in 2025-26, not in 2024-25.

items.statement: Ahmedabad International Airport substation project valued at INR21 crores, 70% remaining to be completed, revenue expected in Q2 and Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Almost, almost, close to about 70%.

items.statement: Jharkhand electrification contract worth INR28.41 crores; revenue expected from Q4 FY25 or end of Q3 FY25 after survey completion.
items.quote: We may expect in a Q4 or end of Q3.

items.statement: Typical labor cost is approximately 8-9% of project; transport cost around 1-1.5% of total project cost.
items.quote: So, typically the labor portion comes to approximately, if I am not wrong, it should vary somewhere around 8-9%.

items.statement: No execution risk seen for new Jharkhand projects as company has been doing such projects all its life.
items.quote: Ma'am, we have been doing this kind of projects all our lives.

items.statement: Acquired controlling stake in Peaton Electrical Company Limited, increasing shareholding from 15.23% to up to 60% to leverage manufacturing expertise.
items.quote: We have also strategically acquired a controlling stake Peter Electrical Company Limited, and this is to move forward and expand our foothold in the electrical market. By increasing our shareholding from 15.23% to up to 60%.

items.statement: Eligible to bid for single projects up to INR140 crores currently; targeting average project size of INR50 crores up to INR130-140 crores.
items.quote: Actually, the whole point is that in the past, what completion certificate we had in our hands enables us to quote up to about INR140 crores as a single value order that we can bid for.

items.statement: By end of 2025, with three completion certificates of ~INR100-130 crores, will be qualified to bid for single projects of INR350 crores.
items.quote: So, when we have three completions of that volume, we will be directly qualified to quote for a single job of INR350 crores.

items.statement: Long-term revenue CAGR guidance of 25% over 5 years
items.quote: remain committed to achieving our long-term CAGR guidance of revenue growth of 25% over a period of 5 years

items.statement: API-Formulation revenue split guidance maintained at 80-20
items.quote: we stand by our long-term guidance of 80/20 with 20% Formulation and 80% API

items.statement: Injectable facility commercialization expected by Q4 FY25
items.quote: by beginning of the quarter 4, we are expecting to take our exhibit batches of some of our products there

items.statement: Plan to launch 8-10 new API products over next 3-4 years focused on oncology, anti-infectives, antibacterial
items.quote: Over the next 3 to 4 years, we plan to introduce 8 to 10 new products in the API space

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 38%, up 63 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins for Q1 FY '25 stood at 38% compared to 37% in Q1 FY '24, a growth of 63 bps year-on-year

items.statement: Q1 FY25 PBT margin (ex-JV) 36.2%, up 285 bps YoY
items.quote: PBT margin stood at 36.2% compared to 33.4%, a jump of 285 bps year-on-year

items.statement: API prices stable across commercial products, no pricing pressure in top products
items.quote: No, not really. So our prices have been stable across the products that we are commercial in

items.statement: API export dip in Japan due to procurement timing, expected to improve in subsequent quarters
items.quote: Japan is one such market where we have seen some bit of dip, and this is again more so from a procurement perspective by some of the companies in Japan which we are seeing getting improved in the subsequent quarters

items.statement: Limbasi facility scaling as planned, many customers buying commercial quantities for regulated markets
items.quote: Many of the customers have already started buying commercial quantities for the regulated markets from the Limbasi facility

items.statement: CDMO opportunities being pursued but no revenue visibility yet, timelines uncertain
items.quote: since nothing has right now, we don't have clarity in terms of what the timelines could be, it will be difficult for us to give the same to you as well

items.statement: Formulation plant utilization 24% vs 20% last year, Limbasi facility utilization 38% vs 34% last year
items.quote: For Formulation, it's around 24% against 20% last year. And for the Limbasi facilities, it is 38% against 34% last year

items.statement: Domestic formulation business growing strongly in critical care, nephrology, rheumatology with 150+ sales team
items.quote: Our Domestic business, particularly in critical care, nephrology and rheumatology has been experiencing strong growth. We have also expanded our sales and distribution network across the domestic market with a team of over 150 people

items.statement: Annual API and Formulation guidance expected to be met despite Q1 seasonality
items.quote: on an annual basis, we expect to meet our guidance

items.statement: Added 21 new formulation products in past year, more planned
items.quote: Over the past financial year, we have added 21 new products to our Formulation portfolio and plan to introduce more throughout the year

items.statement: Global fermentation competition shrinking due to consolidation, creating market share opportunities
items.quote: this segment which is fermentation, we are seeing a lot of consolidation happening. CONCORD BIOTECH Biotecf for So more and more companies are shutting down, which gives us an opportunity to make more gains and inroads into gaining market

items.statement: Management targets INR 600 crores revenue for FY25 with EBITDA margin in the 9%-10% range.
items.quote: We are expecting a topline of INR 600 crores, that we have communicated in the last conference also. So, we are targeting the same.

items.statement: Capex budget of INR 45-55 crores per year for FY25 and FY26 allocated to Unit 8, Unit 9, and expansion of Units 6 and 7, funded from internal accruals.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have outlined a capex budget of INR 45 -55 crores per year for FY25 a nd FY26. This budget will be allocated towards the new unit in Maharashtra & Bharuch, i.e., Unit 8 and Unit 9, as well as the continued expansion of Units 6 and 7.

items.statement: Unit 8 Phase 1 capex of INR 40-45 crores targeted for completion by Q4 FY25 and commissioning in Q1 FY26, with revenue potential of INR 150 crores in FY26 and INR 400 crores at full capacity.
items.quote: Phase 1 involves a capex of INR 40 -45 crores, which includes the purchase of land and civil work, with completion targeted for Q4FY2 025 and commissioning in Q1 of FY26. We expect a gradual ramp -up of capacity over FY26 and FY27, aiming to achieve revenue of around INR 150 crores with the initial investment.

items.statement: Metal Drum demand exceeds current capacity; unable to fulfil all orders, expansion to 70,000 units/month by September 2024.
items.quote: At the moment, we're unable to fulfil all orders, while we have the demand.

items.statement: Raw material prices stable for last few months; pricing norms reflect raw material changes with a lag due to 45-day inventory; stable prices expected to improve margins in coming quarters.
items.quote: But now, as we have seen, the prices are stable in the range from last few months, so we expect results to improve further in coming quarters.

items.statement: IBC export demand impacted by sharp freight cost increase; Line 2 commissioning rescheduled to end of FY25; expect 20% IBC volume growth.
items.quote: However, the recent sharp increase in freight s has impacted demand, particularly in export markets. So, considering these challenges, we have decided to reschedule the commissioning of Line 2 of IBC to the end of FY25.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue mix: Polymer 52%, IBC 36%, Metal Drum 12%; FY25 target mix: Polymer 50%, IBC 38%, Metal Drum 14%.
items.quote: We are expecting that the Polymer Drum will be 50%, IBC will contribute 38% and after that, I think Metal Drum will be around 14% this year.

items.statement: Competitor capacity expansion in IBC acknowledged; management believes market growth will absorb capacity and margins will sustain at 14% EBITDA.
items.quote: We are expanding our business and the competitor is also increasing capacity. New players will also come. So completion will always be there in the business. Despite so many players we get the margin.

items.statement: Unit 6 Metal Drum capacity increased from 30,000 to 50,000/month via automation; target 70,000/month by September 2024, scalable to 90,000.
items.quote: we have significantly increased our Metal Drum production capacity from 30,000 to 50,000 per month and this expansion was driven by automation, which has not only boosted our capacity but also enhanced our operational efficiency.

items.statement: Unit 7 IBC Line 1 operating at 50% utilization; Line 2 commissioning delayed to end of FY25; land for Unit 8 merged into Unit 7 for IBC and Polymer Drum expansion.
items.quote: we are currently operating at 50% capacity utilising on Line 1 of our Intermediate Bulk Containers (IBC). However, the recent sharp increase in freight s has impacted demand, particularly in export markets. So, considering these challenges, we have decided to reschedule the commissioning of Line 2 of IBC to the end of FY25.

items.statement: EPR liability of INR 75-100 lakhs per year to be saved through in-house recycling at Unit 9.
items.quote: Our EPR liability for a year comes to around INR 1 crore. Around INR 7500000 to INR 1 crore. That will be saved.

items.statement: Volume growth of 14% YoY in Q1 FY25 across all three verticals; total income INR 133.6 crores.
items.quote: Our overall volume increased by 14% year-on-year, driven by strong growth across all three of our verticals. We ended the quarter with a total income of INR 133.6 crores.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20% on conservative side for FY25
items.quote: Revenue will be in growth, between 15% to 20% on a conservative side.

items.statement: Order book of Rs. 4,915 crores as of June 2024 plus Rs. 510 crores new orders after June
items.quote: Till June 2024, we have an order book of around Rs.4,915 crores. Even after June the company has received Rs. 510 crores of new orders which will be executed in about 24 to 27 months.

items.statement: New orders awarded worth Rs. 943.48 crores in current financial year
items.quote: I am pleased to report that during the current financial year, our company was awarded new orders worth Rs. 943.48 crores.

items.statement: Robust pipeline of Rs. 5,000 crores with historic conversion rate of 17% to 18%
items.quote: Furthermore, we have a strong prospective pipeline with new bidding orders worth approximately Rs. 5,000 crores, likely to be decided in the coming months.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 13.09% in Q1 FY25, up 137 bps YoY, management expects margins to improve further
items.quote: Margin is better and will be better. And EBITDA will be better.

items.statement: Annual capex guidance of around Rs. 30 crores
items.quote: My CAPEX is around Rs. 30 crores annually.

items.statement: Railway orders target to reach 25% of order book from current ~17%
items.quote: We are expecting to cover our order book up to 25%.

items.statement: Debtor days increased to ~166 due to election delays, expected to normalize to 60-70 days in 3-4 months
items.quote: Due to the union elections, the payments were slowed down by the department. So, now, it will take 3 -4 months f or all the cycle to be set up

items.statement: Backward integration with RMC plants, crusher units, hot mix plants reducing project costs
items.quote: With these in-house manufacturing capacities we are able to considerably reduce the Project Cost without any compromise to its quality.

items.statement: Water sector opportunities abundant with Jal Jeevan Mission budget of Rs. 98,700 crores and AMRUT 2.0 allocation of Rs. 8,000 crores
items.quote: As we have seen in the Union budget, the Ministry of Jal Shakti has announced budget of 98,700 crores for Jal Jeevan mission. Since this is a basic utility project the consistency is going to remain, like the Jal Jeevan mission, similarly 8000 crores are allotted for Amrut 2.0.

items.statement: Geographic expansion into Goa, targeting Tamil Nadu and Telangana, planning entry into Andhra Pradesh and Bihar
items.quote: we have done water treatment plan t in Goa. We have been in Goa. And our target is in Tamil Nadu. And our next target is Telangana

items.statement: No tender cancellations or challenges from new Rajasthan government despite market rumors
items.quote: No, this has not happened.

items.statement: Sufficient funds for current order book, no requirement for QIP until next year
items.quote: No sir, as of now, we have sufficient money for the company's order book. We don't have any requirement till next year.

items.statement: Revenue seasonality: Q1 10-15%, Q2 20%, Q3 35%, Q4 45% of annual revenue
items.quote: Initially, it is in quarter one, 10% to 15%, next is 20, next is 35 and remaining in Q4.

items.statement: Working capital requirement for water supply projects 10% to 15% initially
items.quote: Sir, in water supply project, working capital requirement is between10% to 15% initially.

items.statement: Gross bookings growth revised to 10-15% from prior 15-20% due to flat B2C outlook
items.quote: Our sense is that B2C will actually be closer to flat which means growth rates will be between the 10 % and 15% mark as opposed to the 15 % to 20% mark in terms of gross bookings.

items.statement: Air bookings growth expected ~10%, hotels ~20% after base effect normalizes
items.quote: Air should be again - air will be closer to 10. Hotels after this base effect gets adjusted, should be closer to 20.

items.statement: 34 new corporate accounts added with INR 2,028 million annual billing potential
items.quote: The company successfully secured 34 new corporate customer accounts representing an annual billing potential of INR2,028 million with average billing potential up 77% sequentially.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA INR 105 million vs INR 173 million YoY; ex-new initiatives would be ~INR 145 million
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA came in at INR105 million, a decrease from INR 173 million in the same period last year partly reflecting the lower volumes in the B2C space and partly due to the added cost of onboarding the new teams for the initiatives that I just spoke about.

items.statement: Hired ~80-90 people for MICE, mid-market, visa, expense management costing ~INR 40 million in quarter
items.quote: The cost of such incremental hire is close to INR40 million and this is for the quarter. There is a team of over 80 people that's being hired.

items.statement: Corporate travel growing; IT sector travel spend down ~30% vs pre-COVID but outperforming industry ~50% decline
items.quote: While travel spend on the Yatra platform by IT services customers was approximately 30 % down versus pre-COVID levels, industry reports that we've seen recently indicate a nearly 50% decline in overall IT services travel spend compared to pre -COVID.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted to 55% B2B / 45% B2C from historical 55-60% B2C
items.quote: We are now getting to a situation where we are seeing 55% odd coming from the corporate side, from the B2B side of things.

items.statement: Take rate may decline 30-50 bps due to mix shift but net revenue retention should improve
items.quote: in my sense, if I just do a quick math on that would be in the 30 to 50 basis points kind of change at the overall take rate level, but in terms of the net revenue flow through that should improve on account of the higher mix of corporate.

items.statement: IndiGo offering exclusive discounted fares on own channels raising B2C customer acquisition costs
items.quote: Over the past few months and particularly in the last quarter, we've seen the country's largest airline begin to offer deeply discounted fares exclusively on its website and B2C mobile app.

items.statement: Supply constraints from IndiGo's 75+ grounded aircraft intensifying B2C competition
items.quote: One is obviously the supply side constraint that has come on account of Indigo's 75-plus aircrafts getting out of circulation for the engine repair issue.

items.statement: Expense management pilot (RECAP) with positive feedback; meaningful revenue in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: It will take us maybe another three to four months before we can actually say that now we are able to generate revenue from this at a meaningful level or at least the trendline is getting to a meaningful stage

items.statement: Streamlined ~100 positions in non-corporate businesses; benefits from September
items.quote: we've streamlined almost 100 positions and the benefits of this should start flowing through in the month of September after accounting for any notice period obligations.

items.statement: Cash and term deposits INR 4.4 billion; gross debt reduced to INR 210 million from INR 1.7 billion YoY
items.value: INR 4.4 billion cash, INR 210 million debt
items.quote: Lastly as of 30th June, we were carrying cash and cash equivalents and term deposits on our books of INR4.4 billion. Our gross debt is down to our lowest level of INR210 million compared to INR1.7 billion year-ago same period.

items.statement: Cumulative refurbishment capex for Grand Hyatt Mumbai and Delhi is around INR 100 crores, partly spent, remainder in coming quarters.
items.quote: So, on a cumulative basis, the capex for the refurb would be around INR100 crores. Part of it is already expended. There is only a part which will come in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Phase 2 expansion of 317 keys at Grand Hyatt Mumbai to start construction in FY26, taking 18 months to complete.
items.quote: And the phase two is to add the key count on top of Grand Hyatt. And we are on track, as I said commencing in FY26, and it will take 18 -odd months for completion.

items.statement: No formal EBITDA margin guidance given; margins expected to improve as refurb disruption ends, non-recurring costs normalize, and renewable power sourcing resumes.
items.quote: So, look, we don't give guidance. But generally, I can talk about trends. And as I was saying, one of the key factors which has impacted, the margins is there are two or three things, one of them being the refurb and the disruption impact, which, as I said, in the next few quarters will go away.

items.statement: ARR remains robust in July with Grand Hyatt Mumbai up 30% YoY, Delhi up 19% YoY, Lucknow up 19% YoY; occupancy expected to recover in stronger seasonal quarters.
items.quote: In July Grand Hyatt, we've seen a 30% uptick in ARR. And Delhi continues to be very, very strong at 19%, even in July. And Lucknow is also seeing a 19% growth in the month of July from a variance perspective on ARRs (YoY).

items.statement: Expect double-digit overall revenue growth in FY25 driven primarily by ARR growth with occupancy recovery.
items.quote: So, I would say that we would achieve with a combination of recovery of occupancy and ARRs, we should see double digit overall growth primarily driven by ARRs.

items.statement: Committed to adding 1,000 keys over next three years, primarily from ROFO assets; inorganic acquisitions outside ROFO also being pursued to augment this target.
items.quote: We are totally committed, and we are continuing to put in place the strategy for adding 1,000 rooms over the next three years. And in addition to that we also are striving to add further key counts to inorganic growth on top of the 1,000 keys that we had earlier shared with all of you.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai relaunch by mid-November 2024 with fully refurbished rooms, new Grand Club, two upgraded F&B outlets, and new 'Showroom' event venue opening September 2024.
items.quote: So in all if you have to see Grand Hyatt Bombay at the end of the year which is mid-November that's what we're taking. W e will have a new product to go in the market and actually further strengthen our rates and occupancy and attract the business that we're looking to get in

items.statement: Construction of 317 new keys atop Grand Hyatt Mumbai will take ~98 rooms out of inventory on rotational basis during build phase.
items.quote: Having said that, we have taken account of 100 rooms, about 98 odd rooms which will go out of inventory on a rotational basis while the structure is being constructed on the building.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 asset EBITDA grew 2% YoY on like-to-like basis; consolidated EBITDA stable at INR 68 crores despite refurb impact and INR 4-5 crores non-recurring R&M costs.
items.quote: We've seen 19% growth Y-o-Y on operating revenues and EBITDA we've achieved stability in EBITDA, wherein EBITDA is stable at INR 68 crores. And if you net out the other income at INR63 crores it's at the same level as it was in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Luxury portfolio ARR grew 11% YoY in Q1 FY25 to INR 11,686; consolidated portfolio ARR up 7% YoY; both Grand Hyatt and rest of portfolio outperformed comp set on ARR.
items.quote: On the key performance matrix, we've seen very strong performance on ARR, where our consolidated portfolio in Q1 saw a 7% Y -o-Y increase in ARR, driven primarily by our luxury portfolio of assets, which saw 11% Y -o-Y growth in ARR in the Q1FY25 to 11,686 from INR10,564 in Q1FY24.

items.statement: Repaid INR 1,500 crores debt from IPO proceeds; net debt-to-equity improved to 0.17x from 5.94x YoY; cash balance INR 350 crores as of June 2024.
items.quote: We've seen revenues touching INR 204 crores in quarter one, which is a 21% Y-o-Y growth despite the disruption in Mumbai and the normal slackness in the general Mumbai market that we saw last quarter. But importantly, the PBT has grown by 2x quarter on quarter. As you all know that fourth quarter is normally the strongest quarter. We've seen on a quarter-on-quarter basis 2x growth in profit before

items.statement: Expect stronger organic growth in International Business in Q2 FY25 compared to Q2 FY24
items.quote: We expect to see stronger organic growth in International Business in Q2 FY25 compared to Q2 FY24.

items.statement: Project full-year effective tax rate around 17.5%
items.quote: So, yes, the current quarter, the tax rate is coming at 19%, but on a full-year basis, we project it at around 17.5 %.

items.statement: Expect full-year depreciation and amortization expense around INR 55 Crore
items.quote: However, on a full year basis, on the expected capitalization that we are looking at in the current year, the overall depreciation and amortization expense for the full year should be around INR 55 Crore.

items.statement: Wage hikes effective from July, will impact Q2 costs
items.quote: So, our increment cycle works from July to June, so increments happen in the month of July. So, that gets effective from July month.

items.statement: Jumbonline generated GTV of INR 814 Crores and revenue of INR 32 Crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The business generated a GTV of INR 814 Crores and a revenue of INR 32 Crores.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin 20.33% and PAT margin 14.56% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins and PAT margins for the quarter stood at 20.33% and 14.56%, respectively.

items.statement: Gross profit as percentage of GTV improved from 3.22% to 3.52% year on year
items.quote: Gross profits as a percentage of GTV for the qua rter improved from 3.22% to 3.5 2% on year on year basis

items.statement: Take rate improvement primarily from mix shift, not from increasing take rates in any region
items.quote: So, yes, as the mix of GTV changes and shifts from one particular region to other, there could be minor improvements in the take rate, but it would primarily be coming from the mix impact rather than we increasing our take rates or gross profits in any particular region

items.statement: Expect future growth to be more volume driven than price driven as pricing softens
items.quote: I think Jeet, our view is that at this point it is going to be more volume driven than just the average transaction value driven because there are already some correction starting to happen in pricing, right.

items.statement: Non-airline business share grew from 46% in Q1 FY24 to 57% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The share of non -airline business grew from 46% in Q 1 FY24 to 57% in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Hotel look-to-book ratio improved to 8.72% from 8.07% a year ago for international business
items.quote: Q1 for the international business , our look - to-book ratio stood at 8.72% compared to 8.07% a year ago

items.statement: Not seeing immediate softness from Middle East tensions; travel resilient unless very adverse event occurs
items.quote: We are not seeing any immediate softness because of the political situation in the Middle East. Historically, we have seen that unless some very-very adverse event happens, like what happened October 7 last year, which caused a temporary blip in the Israel source market.

items.statement: Integration of Jumbonline progressing well; expect significant part completed before end of financial year
items.quote: We expect to complete a significant part of the integration before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: International business organic GTV grew 17% year on year excluding Jumbonline
items.quote: So, the international business GTV on an organic ba sis without including the Jumbonline business grew by 17% year on year

items.statement: India hotel and ancillaries GTV grew 2.3% despite market de-growth; could have been double-digit without elections and Maldives disruption
items.quote: In our Hotel and Ancillaries Business, we achieved a 2.3% growth in GTV despite market de-growth. However, we faced some challenges this quarter including the impact of general elections and disruptions of the Maldives b usiness, which notably affected our performance. With out TBO Tek Limited Aug 13th, 2024 these challenges, we believe our growth could have reached double digit growth

items.statement: Export demand remains sluggish; commodity chemical prices expected to stay subdued due to excessive dumping.
items.quote: In the coming months, we expect commodity chemical prices to remain subdued due to excessive dumping at low prices, while specialty chemicals are anticipated to perform with a stable pricing situation and added volumes.

items.statement: Management refrains from giving revenue or margin guidance due to immense uncertainty in the global geopolitical environment.
items.quote: In terms of guidance what you are asking for, we generally would refrain from giving any guidance number, and don't want to mislead any investors due to immense uncertainty in the global geopolitical environment.

items.statement: CPVC capacity doubled and running at 100% production in Q1; SIOP capacity completed in May, ramping up with full benefits expected from H2.
items.quote: The CPVC capacity was completed on time, with production ramping up from Quarter 3 of last year, we are happy to state that Q1 was the 1st Quarter with 100% production at the new capacity.

items.statement: Renewable energy project on track for completion in H2 FY25.
items.quote: Our investment in the renewable energy project is also underway and is on track for expected completion in H2.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals EBITDA contribution doubled year-on-year; chlorine internal consumption increased to 70% from 65%, targeting chlorine neutrality by FY26.
items.quote: EBITDA contribution of our specialty chemicals to our business has increased two-fold year-on-year, despite minor corrections in realizations.

items.statement: Specialty segment EBITDA margins stable at 36%; commodity segment EBITDA dropped sharply due to falling prices.
items.quote: The EBITDA margins for the specialty segment dropped firm at 36% as against 33% in Quarter 1 of FY24.

items.statement: Caustic soda prices have bottomed out with no scope for further reduction or increase; PVC prices firm in Q1 but correcting in Q2.
items.quote: Frankly, there is no scope for any further reduction in the prices of caustic soda, whether internationally or local, because chlorine itself is under tremendous pressure.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on CPVC imports from China and Korea recommended for continuation; expected notification before expiry in last week of August.
items.quote: Already the Commerce Ministry has recommended continuation of the anti-dumping duty in a definitive, with the definitive duties on China and Korea, and we are waiting for their notification from the finance ministry.

items.statement: CPVC margins unlikely to move higher despite anti-dumping duty; expected to remain in mid-30% range as duties are for industry protection, not profiteering.
items.quote: Yes, it will remain in the same range. We don't foresee, you see anti-dumping duties are not for profiteering

items.statement: Synthetic rutile export demand sluggish due to global volatility and China demand situation; green shoots expected from H2 but later than anticipated.
items.quote: Global volatility and demand situation in China has put significant pressure on exports of synthetic rutile in both volume and price. However, we are seeing some green shoots from H2 of this year.

items.statement: Caustic soda production to increase by ~15% within next month, targeting full capacity of 250-260 tonnes per day.
items.quote: Within the next one month we will be working to almost increase by about 15% increase in our production now, and in very short time we will be running to our whole capacity, which will be about 250 to 260 tonnes per day.

items.statement: Q2 profitability expected to face more pressure due to PVC price corrections; specialty chemicals expected to improve slightly.
items.quote: This quarter, that is Quarter 2 we don't see any major shift of profitability or profitability for the company as a whole. In fact, we see more pressure in the profitability for Quarter 2.

items.statement: SIOP sales seasonal; Q1 volumes lower due to seasonality and freight rates, but up 80% year-on-year; full benefits from new capacity expected from H2.
items.quote: We expect gradual increase in sales and full benefits to accrue from this from H2 onwards.

items.statement: Current CPVC prices around $830-850 import parity (Rs.70,000-78,000 ex-works), down ~Rs.8,000 from last month; blended CPVC ~Rs.150,000.
items.quote: CPVC current prices are around $850 import parity, $830, $850 which is around Rs.70,000, Rs.77,000, Rs.78,000 ex-works, which is almost Rs.8000 lower than what it was in the last month.

items.statement: Annual EBITDA guidance of INR 2,000 crores with potential 10% upside to INR 2,200 crores given current prices and upcoming volumes from Aseptic and Egypt PET chips plant
items.quote: And our annual EBITDA guidance, which I had earlier said, about INR2,000 crores, I think there could be an upside by another 10% given the prices today as well as the Q4 when we see the impact of the larger volumes from the Aseptic Packaging division coming into play, and our plant in Egypt for the PET chips getting commissioned

items.statement: Offshore packaging films margin improved to 13.4% in Q1 FY25 vs 12.6% in Q4 FY24 and 7.2% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: And the offshore business as such has reported a 13.4% margin vis-a-vis 12.6% margin in the Q4 versus 7.2% margin in Q1 of the same period, Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: India packaging films volumes grew 5% sequentially; overseas volumes flat with 1% offtake increase
items.quote: Notable is that in India, even on a sequential quarter basis, we have seen volumes going up by 5%, which is very healthy for the packaging films business of ours. And overseas, if we see, has largely been flat on a sequential basis. The offtake has gone up just by 1%

items.statement: Egypt PET chips plant to be operational by Q3-Q4 FY25 before next financial year; Aseptic debottlenecking before January 2025 season; Mexico CPP facility commissioning in Q2 FY25
items.quote: As we'll go through the rest of the financial year, I think we are due to complete our PET chips in Egypt, which will probably happen in Q3, Q4 at the best, but certainly before the next financial year begins, I think we'll make this plant operational. Aseptic debottlenecking will happen probably before the season starts in January of '25 now, and the Mexico CPP facility will be commissioned proba

items.statement: Panipat PET chips plant achieved 65% capacity utilization in Q1, selling ~25,000 tons with 30% bottle grade (100% external) and 70% film grade (55% captive, 45% external)
items.quote: The India PET chips started from April. We capitalized this plant on 31st of March, and the first quarter itself, the capacity utilization achievement is about 65%. We sold about 25,000-odd tons, of which 30% was bottle grade, which was -- again, we don't consume it ourselves.

items.statement: Aseptic Packaging recorded highest-ever production and sales at 120% capacity utilization (~8.5 billion packs annualized); targeting 60% domestic / 40% export mix at full 12 billion packs capacity
items.quote: Aseptic Packaging, this was the quarter where we recorded the highest-ever production and the sales, equivalent to capacity utilization level of about 120% for the quarter. As I said earlier, we will have a higher capacity available - 12 billion packs, but current capacity utilization as at 120% tantamount to about 8.5 billion packs annualized capacity.

items.statement: Currency translation loss of INR 180 crores in Q1 (Nigeria INR 100 cr, Egypt INR 30 cr, Mexico INR 50 cr) described as recurring notional phenomenon from consolidating foreign subsidiaries
items.quote: This quarter, again, we had a currency loss of INR180 crores, of which Nigeria was about INR100 crores, Egypt was INR30 crores and Mexico was around INR50 crores. I think this has become quite a normal phenomenon, because as you translate th eir local currency balance sheets into Indian rupee, that translation losses do result in these losses, which are more or less notional

items.statement: Recycling PCR opportunity emerging with regulations from April 2025; ~$40 million invested across Egypt, Mexico, India; plants functioning but not at full capacity; margins expected to improve as regulation drives demand
items.quote: PCR we might have expensed around 15 million in Egypt, around 15 million in Mexico and remaining smaller places 10 million. So, around 40 million expenses overall. Yash Dedhia: So, these all capacities are ready to function? Rajesh Bhatia: No, they are already functioning. We're saying that they'll get impetus with the law. So today, it is a self-regulation. So, when it is the self-regulation then

items.statement: Full-year VNB margin guidance 25-26% and mid-teens VNB growth, but dynamic due to surrender regulation changes
items.quote: My guidance was for the year, we will outlook anywhere between 25% and 26% margin as against 26.5% last year. And the forecast was we will have teen kind of VNB growth for the year now.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 VNB margin 17.5%, down from prior year due to tactical ULIP push; expect improvement as operating leverage kicks in
items.quote: Increased ULIP and lower non-PAR contribution result in Q1 FY25 in VNB of 17.5 % lower than previous year. However, VNB grew by 3% and as we go long, VNB is going to be a key measure.

items.statement: Surrender regulation changes estimated to impact company-level margin by 100-200 bps during transitory period; aim to mitigate over 3-6 months
items.quote: We estimate that the surrender impact will be in the range of 100-200 basis points at the company level for the transitory period and we will work hard at figuring out more ideas so that we are able to tie through these changes unaffected.

items.statement: Individual adjusted first-year premium grew 27% in Q1 FY25, accelerated to 32% YTD July; proprietary channels grew 60%, now 49% of sales
items.quote: On full year, individual adjusted first year premium basis, we saw a growth of robust 27% outpacing both the private sector and overall industry growth rates of 24% and 20% respectively for Q1 FY25. I am very happy to share that July numbers just came out and this number has accelerated further for the month ending July YTD. Our growth has increased from 27% to 32%.

items.statement: ULIP share of total APE rose from 25% to 39% in Q1 FY25 driven by e-commerce; retail protection up 53%, credit protection up 49%
items.quote: This launch led to more than 100% growth in ULIP segment, shifting our product mix towards this segment from 25% total APE to 39% of APE in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Axis Bank bancassurance grew 19% YTD July (45% in July alone); counter share stable at 65-70%
items.quote: By the time we finished July, we are seeing about 19% growth from Axis Bank.

items.statement: Policyholder OPEX-to-GWP 17.9%, total cost-to-GWP 26.3%; OPEX grew 14% due to distribution headcount increase
items.quote: Policyholder OPEX -to-GWP is 17.9% and total cost -to-GWP is 26.3%. Policyholder OPEX has grown by 14%, largely due to increase in headcount in the distribution function.

items.statement: Value of new business (VNB) Rs 254 crore in Q1 FY25, up 3% YoY; embedded value Rs 22,043 crore aided by Axis capital infusion of Rs 1,612 crore
items.quote: The value of new business , stands at Rs. 254 crore s for the quarter in comparison with Rs.247 crores last year with an NBM of 17.5%.

items.statement: Surrender regulation changes require product refiling by 30 Sept; phasing replacement from 15 Aug; assume some surrender increase in 100-200 bps estimate
items.quote: We have a phasing approach. We will begin replacing our products somewhere from 15th of August to 30th of September in different tranches.

items.statement: Solvency margin 203% post Axis capital infusion; AUM crossed Rs 1.61 lakh crore, up 25% YoY
items.quote: With the infusion of capital, which was completed during the quarter, the solvency margin stands now at 203% as at end of June '24.

items.statement: 13th month persistency (premium basis) highest ever at 87%, up ~320 bps; 61st month persistency 58%
items.quote: In terms of premium our 13th month persistency for regular and limited pay premium reached its highest ever at 87% and improvement above ~320 basis points, while our 61st first month persistency stood at 58% for the period ending June 2024.

items.statement: Agent count 1,06,860 at June 2024; focus on activation and top-performing agents rather than total count
items.quote: The agent headcount at June '24 end, 1,06,860.

items.statement: eCommerce channel 37% of proprietary sales in Q1 FY25 (vs 20% last year); direct channel ~18% (vs 20% last year)
items.quote: So, 20% eCommerce within the proprietary sales which she mentioned 37% for this quarter, that number was 20% last year.

items.statement: Operating leverage will improve margins each quarter even at same product mix; Q1 typically 17-21% margin range historically
items.quote: If your question is that even if I run the same product mix that I ran in Q1 and Q2, will the margins improve? Answer is yes.

items.statement: Non-operating variance positive Rs 276 crore in Q1 from equity and debt markets; operating variance also positive from persistency and mortality
items.quote: Further, the non-operating variance stands at Rs. 276 crores, due to movements in interest rates and the equity market.

items.statement: Axis emerging verticals ~10% of Axis sales; agency new models ~5% of agency channel; both growing fast
items.quote: It will be around 10% from an Axis perspective, around 5% for the agency channel for today.

items.statement: Management expects low double-digit top-line growth and mid-teens EBITDA pre-ESOP margin by end of FY25
items.quote: we are on course to deliver what we have guided, which is a top line of low double digits and maintained EBITDA exit for this year

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA pre-ESOP margin reached 12.4%, up from 2.8% in Q1 FY24 and 11.4% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: On a Y-o-Y basis, the increase is 9.60% from 2.8% in Q1 financial year '24 to 12.4% in Q1 financial year '25. And on a quarter-on-quarter basis, the increase is about 1% from 11.4% in Q4 financial year '24 to 12.4% in Q1 '25

items.statement: Gross margin improved 360 bps YoY to 45.1% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our gross margins has improved by 3.60 percentage, rising from 41.5% in Q1 financial year '24 to 45.1% in Q1 financial year '25

items.statement: Operating expenses reduced 1.1% YoY despite global inflationary pressures
items.quote: We have managed to achieve a 1.1% reduction in our opex on a Y-o-Y basis. That is INR1,291 million in Q1 financial year '24, to million in Q1 financial year '25

items.statement: Emerging markets revenue grew 36% YoY in constant currency, led by price actions in Turkey
items.quote: Emerging markets reported revenue of INR1,187 million, marking a 36% year-on-year growth in constant currency terms. This increase were driven by the decisive price actions estimated in Turkey

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected to be subdued at INR 50-60 crore
items.quote: the capex for the current year is going to be subdued, but it's supposed to be around INR50 crores to INR60 crores for the current financial year across the board

items.statement: Turkey market improving but still volatile; management remains agile on pricing and volume actions
items.quote: while things are substantially better than what they were a year ago, we have to still be very agile, and we are taking the right kind of actions on pricing and volume in that market

items.statement: Promoter remains supportive; M&A may use alternative structures not requiring balance sheet funding
items.quote: we have a very committed investor with us and our -- and there is nothing that's prevent us from taking any advantage of any opportunity which comes through a different model, yes. So our principal promoter continues to be very supportive

items.statement: Working capital days elevated at 110-120 due to geographic spread, logistics delays; expected to improve gradually
items.quote: we must resume the working capital to be range bound. I'm going down gradually as the situation improves or eases. That's how we are looking at the situation as of now

items.statement: U.S. FDA project on hold for next 12-24 months; lower priority vs other growing markets
items.quote: from a short-term point of view, which I would say is the next 12 to 24 months, it's unlikely that we will do any kind of acceleration on the U.S. project

items.statement: Turkey exports nearly doubled in Q1; target to match export value to import value in 12-18 months for natural FX hedge
items.quote: in first quarter, I think we have almost doubled the business versus the same time last quarter. I've indicated in the past broadly that we, today, export about 50% of what we import equivalent value, and that is something we intend to neutralize and make our exports equal to imports in the next 12 to 18 months

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance revised to 15-20% for FY25 from earlier 20-25%
items.quote: No. So, I think the guidance, which I would have, is probably more like 15% to 20% on a top line growth.

items.statement: Expects double-digit EBITDA margins by late H2 FY25, sustainable 11-13% in 3 years
items.quote: As I said before, I think we definitely continue to hold our guidance in the same spread that we will get into double -digit EBITDA margins.

items.statement: FY25 capex guided at INR 200-250 crores including Chakan Phase 2 and Sanand EV readiness
items.quote: For the full year FY '25, we are looking at anywhere between INR 200 crores to INR250 crores capex.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of INR 80-100 crores per year across facilities and R&D
items.quote: So, the maintenance capex would be close to around INR 80 crores to INR100 crores, which is our usual capex.

items.statement: Order book of INR 2,300-2,400 crores with 88% LED, 43% EV, 67% passenger vehicles
items.quote: Currently, we have a robust order book of approximately INR2,300 crores, with 88% dedicated to LED light.

items.statement: 40-50% of order book to convert in FY25 (mostly H2), 40% in FY26, 10% in FY27
items.quote: So, I would say that in FY '25, we will see almost close to 40% to 50% of this, and most of this will come in H2.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 9.1% (+40bps YoY), PAT margin 4.5% (+80bps YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q1 FY '25 stood at 9.1%, a growth of 40 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margins hover 7-8.2%; Q1 manufacturing EBITDA fell to 8.4% from 10.4% in Q4
items.quote: If you look at the manufacturing EBITDA, it was at 10.4% in quarter 4, which has come to 8.4% in quarter 1.

items.statement: Material margin under pressure from higher LED import content (~25% of buying value); PCB localization to benefit FY26
items.quote: So about 25% of the total buying value would still be imported, which would again be largely driven by the electronic category.

items.statement: Plastic raw material price escalations in Q1; OEM compensation expected with 3-6 month lag
items.quote: Second, there are certain price escalations, specifically on plastic raw materials, which we have seen in quarter one. And obviously, our buying has gone up in terms of the value. We are under discussions with the OEMs to get compensated.

items.statement: Passenger vehicle industry growth seen at 3-5% in FY25; Q2 demand similar to weak Q1
items.quote: I think most analysts have predicted that their forecast for FY '25 for the passenger vehicle space continues to be in low single digits, anywhere between 3% to 5%.

items.statement: LED share of lighting revenue rose to 45% in Q1 FY25 from 35% YoY; 2-wheeler LED penetration ~50%, 4-wheeler ~55%
items.quote: the share of LED lighting stands at 45% compared to 35% in quarter 1 FY '24, an increase of 1,000 bps

items.statement: 2-wheeler revenue share expected to stabilize at ~1/3 of total; order book 30% 2-wheeler, 70% PV+CV
items.quote: I would expect our 2-wheeler kitty should be around 1/3 of the total pie even going forward, perhaps in not just FY '25, but even in FY '26.

items.statement: Chakan Phase 1 utilization only 55-60% due to XUV700 volumes halving to 4,000-4,500/month from 7,000-8,000
items.quote: Today, my capacity is utilized in Chakan, new facility is just about 60% or 55%.

items.statement: Chakan Phase 2 timeline on track for Q1 FY26 but capex may be pruned to optimize existing capacity first
items.quote: the Phase 2 expansion in terms of a timeline continues to be on track because these are for certain models of OEMs, like Volkswagen and Tata Motors, and the model launches have not been delayed. So, we need to continue from a timeline perspective. However, as mentioned before, the capex outlook would be relooked at to prune down the capex because we will try to optimize our existing capacity befor

items.statement: Sanand Gujarat subsidy INR 10 crores/year until FY28; Maharashtra Chakan subsidy not yet approved
items.quote: Sanand concerned the per month subsidy, i.e., the per annum subsidy is around INR10 crores. Pratik Kothari: This is for how long? Sanjay Mehta: It is up to '27- '28 financial year. It is for 10 years

items.statement: Capex guidance maintained at Rs 5,000 crore plus minus 10% for FY25, reassessing due to closed acquisitions
items.quote: Our CAPEX guidance remains the same at Rs. 5,000 crores plus minus 10%. However, with all the acquisitions closed and in light of the increased business parameter that we have with these new businesses, we are reassessing this.

items.statement: 18 Greenfield plants announced, two operationalized in India and China, one new plant in Mexico, seven in non-automotive
items.quote: Out of the 18 Greenfields we have announced earlier, two have been operationalized and commenced production in India and China respectively. Additionally, we are adding one new plant in Mexico. I would like to highlight that seven Greenfield plants are being set up in the non-automotive space.

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE at 18% annualized in Q1 FY25, target 40% by end of five-year plan
items.quote: I would like to report that the consolidated ROCE based on Q1FY25 annualized basis is now sitting at 18%. While we have a bit to go towards 40%, we will surely make more progress on this number in coming quarters.

items.statement: Light vehicle production flat YoY globally, growth in India and China offset by softness in Europe, industry forecasts flat or slight de-growth in FY25
items.quote: On the vehicle production side, I want to highlight that the light vehicle production remained largely flat on a year-on-year basis. Significant amounts of growth coming out of India and China is being offset by softness of demand in the developed markets, especially Europe. Some of the industry forecasts are projecting light vehicle production to be flat or even slightly de-grow in fiscal 2025 as

items.statement: Non-automotive target 25% of group revenue, aerospace and consumer electronics gaining traction, medical facility coming up in Chennai
items.quote: the target was always to be 25% business to come from non -automotive. So, of course, as you can see that not just the consumer electronics, even the aerospace and the defense businesses, these are also g rowing quite nicely. We also have a medical facility that is coming up in Chennai

items.statement: Logistics costs increased significantly due to Red Sea crisis and Asian port congestion, leading to longer lead times and higher inventories
items.quote: The logistic costs creeped up significantly due to the Red Sea crisis and congestion at the Asian ports, which resulted in longer lead times and hence higher inventories

items.statement: Enabling resolution taken for potential future capital raise to pursue inorganic opportunities in developed markets
items.quote: We hence thought it is prudent for us to take an enabling resolution for potential capital raise in the future. I would like to thank the team for delivering great results.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex at Rs 1,078 crore, includes new plants for emerging markets and non-automotive diversification
items.quote: Our CAPEX for the quarter was Rs. 1,078 crores. As announced earlier, we are setting up new plants to support growth coming out of

items.statement: Working capital increased due to Red Sea crisis and customer schedule volatility, expected to normalize in H2 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, net debt increased by Rs. 3,000 crores. This is primarily attributed to the M&A closures and increased working capital requirements due to the Red Sea crisis and volatility in customer schedules. The increased working capital expected to normalize in the second half of FY 2025.

items.statement: Issued first dual investment grade bonds of US $350 million, debt neutral transaction, $1.4 billion available from committed undrawn facilities and unrestricted cash
items.quote: During the quarter, we also issued our first dual investment grade bonds of US $350 million being a debt neutral transaction for us. We are comfortable with our debt maturity profile and have access to well diversified set of capital resources with 1.4 billion available from committed and undrawn facilities and also unrestricted cash and cash equivalents.

items.statement: Management does not know if INR 4,000 crore FY25 revenue target will be met due to inflation/deflation uncertainty
items.quote: the actual answer is, we don't know. In this past quarter, it's been -- th e volumes have ramped up to the level that we want. The volumes actually have ramped up to a le vel which should generate at normal levels generate a turnover greater than INR4,000 crores

items.statement: Board authorized up to INR 50 crore investment in KNS Shoe Tech subsidiary via rights issue
items.quote: As a sign of our commitment towards the shoe business, the Board has authorized an investment up to INR50 crores in the wholly owned subsidiary, KNS Shoe Tec h by way of subscribing to the rights issue

items.statement: Ice cream factory relocated from Kundli to Nashik; production expected to start by March 2025
items.quote: Production is expected to commence by March '25, that is the next season.

items.statement: Baddi OTC pharma plant has anchor tenant agreement covering 60-65% of capacity
items.quote: From a volume perspective, I think we mentioned this earlier th at we have an anchor tenant agreement with our customer there, where nearly 60%, 65% of the capacity has been underwritten by our main

items.statement: EBITDA margin above 8% driven by commodity deflation and higher-margin new businesses; not considered sustainable
items.quote: So, the deflation is still there. We are not seeing that it is sustainable yet. So, the margins are better because of deflation. And also the shoe business and the new businesses which we are in are better in terms of margins.

items.statement: Effective tax rate increased to ~25% from 20% last year; expected to remain at 25% going forward
items.quote: The effective tax rate is increased to around 25% as compared to 20% in last quarter -- l ast year. We believe that the effective tax rate will be around 25% hereon

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on volume recovery; unclear if structural or temporary due to elections and base effect
items.quote: It's a little early to judge whether this is a revival of the consumption demand, or a temporary dip caused by the elections and a base effect of the previous year. Suffice to say that we are cautiously optimistic about the future.

items.statement: Shoe business expected to be 5-7% of total turnover in FY25 with better margin profile
items.quote: so that turnover of the shoe business vis-a-vis our ent ire business will remain -- will be around 5% to 7% of the entire business

items.statement: Russian FDA approval for one high-value product pending, expected to take another year, delaying exports to Russia
items.quote: The only appro val that is pending from the Russian FDA that is expected to take another year, thereby dela ying exports to Russia

items.statement: No new OTC pharma customers expected in FY25 due to 8-12 month regulatory gestation period
items.quote: So I don't see us being able to sign on any new customers in th is financial year, and that's what we are building even in our numbers, that we do not expect any new customers to come in, in this financial

items.statement: Depreciation and finance costs at INR 20 crore each for Q1; expected to be mostly steady state
items.quote: Both the finance cost and the depreciation is INR20 crores, INR 20 crores for this quarter. And still we do the round of investment. This will be mostly steady-state now.

items.statement: Warrant proceeds of INR 70-75 crore still in FDs, depressing ROE; capex deployment spread over 12-18 months
items.quote: Even today, in spite of having deferred that money, we have INR 70 crores -- INR70 crores or INR75 crores laying in FDs which has actually depressed our ROE numbers for this quarter.

items.statement: Vanitycase Nasik operating asset merger application to be filed in September 2024; NCLT process expected to complete by September 2025
items.quote: We will file the application to SEBI and Stock Exchanges in the month of September. And we expect that NCLT process will take another year to complete. So, we are hoping by September '25, the entire process will be completed.

items.statement: Core FMCG (non-seasonal) volume growth unclear; management lacks data to generalize across categories
items.quote: Mayur, it's difficult to comment, right? We really do not have that kind of data of being able to make a comparison. And I really do not want to go out on a limb and say that yes, it is seasonal here or the seasonal are coming or that they are not coming.

items.statement: Top line is complete pass-through of raw material and packing material prices; bottom line insulated from inflation/deflation
items.quote: our top line is a complete pass-through especially as far as ra w materials and packing materials is concerned. So, from that perspective, if most of our prices go up, volume, even if the same volume will end up showing a higher turnover, it may not affect our bottom

items.statement: Maintain FY25 pre-sales guidance of INR 2,000 crores
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance of INR 2,000 crores of pre-sales in FY '25.

items.statement: Expect losses in Q2 FY25 due to lower deliveries; H2 FY25 expected to be healthy with full-year profits
items.quote: We anticipate reporting of losses in second quarter of the current year as well due to lower deliveries planned. However, second half of the current financial year is expected to be healthy in terms of deliveries, leading to reported profits for full year FY '25.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 PAT negative INR 5.45 crores due to lower-margin Shubham deliveries and one-off costs
items.quote: PAT for Q1 FY '25 recorded a negative at INR 5.45 crores, vis-a-vis positive INR 10.87 crores in Q1 FY '24. Loss was attributable to revenue booking in lower -margin projects - Ashiana Shubham 4A, Chennai.

items.statement: Shubham Phase 5 realization at INR 6,000/sq ft vs Phase 4A at INR 4,700/sq ft; expect margin expansion going forward
items.quote: So, in Shubham Phase 5, we are realizing about INR 6,000 a square foot as compared to about ,I think, INR 4,700 in Phase 4A and Phase 4B is about INR 5,200. So those increasing sale prices will help margins in those 2 phases.

items.statement: Strategic structural margin issues resolved; expect margin expansion going forward
items.quote: Strategic structural issues that were there, those have been resolved. So majority of the issues have been covered, and we should see margin expansion going up forward.

items.statement: Price increase momentum to continue but at a decreasing rate
items.quote: We expect prices to increase, but increase at a decreasing rate as compared to earlier.

items.statement: Amarah Phase 4 pricing ~25% higher than Phase 3; willing to accept lower velocity for higher realization
items.quote: The realization would be about 25% higher than phase 3 as well. Now with most of the projects sold out, we are gunning for higher realizations. We'll be willing to live with a little lower velocity as compared to previous phases and look to maximize pricing as we go forward in this project.

items.statement: Land prices stabilizing after significant increases; construction costs not down but not rising substantially
