items.statement: Bhiwadi sales picked up with best quarters in long time for Tarang and Town; Gurugram velocity low in Q1 due to no inventory
items.quote: The great part of velocity was Bhiwadi sales have picked up. If you see Ashiana Tarang and Ashiana Town, they've had the two best quarters in the longest time.

items.statement: No supply issues currently due to constrained developer funding; NBFC, FDI, AIF funding limited
items.quote: Right now, I don't see supply issues. And I think the single reason why supply issues are not there because not enough developers have good balance sheets, access to funding, the tap of NBFC money is not there, tap of FDI money is not there.

items.statement: Pivoting business development towards senior living; less cyclical, higher entry barriers, less competition
items.quote: We are pivoting more and more towards senior living as a segment. I think more and more Business Development (BD) will happen in senior living. We find senior living to be less cyclical because there are less players, higher entry barriers, less competition, less chances of oversupply, less speculative buying.

items.statement: Launching Swarang in Chennai (Q3 FY25) as sophisticated senior living; active BD in Panvel, Gurugram, Bengaluru, Greater Noida
items.quote: One in Chennai, Ashiana Swarang, which we are calling sophisticated senior livi ng, we are going to launch which are even more premium position than our current senior living offerings . So that launch will be in Q3 and accordingly, we are also refining our business model.

items.statement: Signed project in Jamshedpur (not in deck); active term sheet for Bengaluru senior living land
items.quote: We have signed a project in Jamshedpur. We have also given the disclosure of the project in Jamshedpur. But we have not captured it on the table in the deck.

items.statement: HSIIDC land parcel launch slipped to Q1 FY26 due to approval delays
items.quote: Prem, we are a little off track. I think it will slip to the first quarter of the next financial year. We've been stuck in a bit of approval there. So I think it will go to the Q1 of next financial year i.e. FY'26.

items.statement: Comfortable taking slightly more leverage given INR 1,700 crores collectible from ongoing projects; temperament remains conservative
items.quote: We are comfortable with taking a little bit more leverage than we have today. But I said we'll continue to be cash rich, keep low debt to equity as compared to industry. The comfort on taking more debt is basically coming from the fact that we have about INR 1,700 crores to collect from ongoing projects itself.

items.statement: No QIP needed currently; comfortable with debt position and cash flows
items.quote: No, we don't have to do QIP right now. There is no need to manage the debt and so we don't need to do QIP . We are very comfortable

items.statement: Full-year profit growth guidance of at least 20% over FY24 base of ~INR1,400 crore
items.quote: Overall, for the year we're giving guidance of a 20% growth over last year's numb er. So last year I think our profit was little less than INR1,400 crores. So, on that, they're saying we'll grow at least

items.statement: Q2 FY25 expected to perform well sequentially similar to Q1
items.quote: I can say Q2 should also do very well. I think like Q1 it should do well.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 expected to perform well on quarter-on-quarter basis
items.quote: I was comparing Q-o-Q. I was comparing this Q1 with Q2 And I'm saying Q2 also we should do well like Q1 is what I am saying.

items.statement: Revlimid market share to ramp from single digit to one-third of US market by January 2026 per agreement
items.quote: We start off with a single digit and we go up to one third of the market before January '26.

items.statement: Agrochem business targets INR250-300 crore branded business in 2-3 years
items.quote: I think my personal view is we have to give it about two years. So, if you give it about two, three years from now, I think you'll probably have a INR250 crores, INR300 crores nice, branded business with a stable income.

items.statement: Kothur warning letter: no new approvals from site; critical filings being moved to Vizag and CMOs to mitigate risk
items.quote: We continue to supply from that plant into the U.S. market. So, it did not stop any of the supplies. In terms of the filings, the impact has been that we are not getting any new approvals from that site.

items.statement: Key execution risk is timely transfer and approval of critical filings from Kothur to avoid losing business opportunity
items.quote: The risk, if anything is, I would say our execution of moving things out and getting it done. I think that's all it, especially the first two files, we have to move them out and get the batches done quickly.

items.statement: Adding API capacity to service external customers and improve internal capability
items.quote: We're trying to add some capacity so that we can service our outside customers and improve our internal capability.

items.statement: Cash balance ~INR2,000 crore post Q1; conserving capital for acquisitions to reduce earnings volatility and expand geographic footprint
items.quote: Without the receivable of Q1 right now we have about INR2,000 crores of cash in our books.

items.statement: No buyback planned currently; conserving cash for potential large acquisitions
items.quote: At this time, we don't have any plans for buyback. But if something changes, obviously we'll speak about it. But at least my thinking now is, no, not currently.

items.statement: Next leg of growth beyond FY26 expected from Semaglutide, Olaparib, Erdafitinib, Imbruvica and new FTF filings; targeting 10 ideas over 8-10 years
items.quote: So, in the next two years if you pull off another three or four FTF or interesting ideas, then y ou have about 10 ideas for the next, let's say eight years. And even if we get half those ideas right, I think you'll do well

items.statement: Subsidiaries (RoW) did INR180 crore revenue with INR43 crore PBT last quarter; normalized run-rate ~INR140-150 crore/quarter
items.quote: The subs, which represent a significant part of our RoW business is doing -- last quarter did about INR180 crores and fairly profitable. So, we had a PBT of INR43 crores.

items.statement: Domestic formulation stable at ~INR100 crore/quarter growing 8-10% YoY ex-one-offs; Semaglutide launch expected March 2026 patent expiry
items.quote: I think the domestic has been stable, we're doing about INR100 crores per quarter. I think that's been fairly stable. If you remo ve the one-off, on an overall base business wise, remember the one-off is growing around 8% to 10

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 12.40% in Q1 FY25, up 65% YoY, driven by product mix
items.quote: Our EBITDA of INR2.80 crores represents an impressive year-on-year growth of 65%, with EBITDA margin improving marginally to 12.40%.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain the current EBITDA margin trend going forward
items.quote: I think we should be able to maintain the trend, ma'am.

items.statement: Product mix improvement is the primary driver of EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: The margin EBITDA improvement is basically on account primarily for the product mix.

items.statement: First phase of expansion requires approximately INR30 crores capex, funded by internal accruals and debt
items.quote: But initially the capex, the first phase of the expansion would need a capex of around INR30 crores. And that would be funded by internal accruals as well as debt initially.

items.statement: Land acquisition for new facility expected to conclude in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Yes, maybe very shortly we should be able to conclude the things. Maybe in 1 or 2 quarters we'll get to know more about it.

items.statement: Order book is typically less than one month due to accessory product nature
items.quote: Ma'am, my order book is usually less than a month because we are in an accessory industry.

items.statement: Export revenue share increased to 19% in Q1 FY25 from 15% in FY24
items.quote: Exports were around 19%.

items.statement: Major growth opportunity seen in export segment and domestic defence sector
items.quote: The major opportunity looks to come from the export segment. And next in the domestic defence and other segments hold a good promise.

items.statement: Export margins are depressed due to competition from China and Taiwan, but volumes are higher
items.quote: No, in exports we definitely have competition from China and Taiwan. So the margins are definitely a little bit depressed, but here we get more volumes as compared to the domestics.

items.statement: BIS quality control order implementation timeline estimated at 1.5-2 years, dependent on government process
items.quote: But safely, you can say 1.5 years to 2 years is something what you can look at such standards coming in.

items.statement: Neoprene business (via subsidiary) expected to generate ~INR2 crores annually initially, with better margins than core business
items.quote: Margin profile would be better. And the expectation is definitely to the tune of around INR2 crores or roughly INR2 crores worth of business per year to start with.

items.statement: Repeat business constitutes 80-85% of revenue; export client conversion takes 5-6 months, domestic 1 month
items.quote: One is, in case of repeat business, we would be having around 80%-85% as a repeat business from our customers.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute ~37% of revenue; top 15 contribute 45-50%
items.quote: Top 10 would contribute to roughly 37% of the revenue.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to BBB-/Stable by CRISIL for ~INR18.3 crores working capital facilities
items.quote: We have now been upgraded to BBB-/Stable for banking facilities, working capital facilities approximately around INR18.3 crores.

items.statement: Working capital cycle averages 2.5-3 months with marginal improvement in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Yes, the average working capital cycle is around 2.5 months to 3 months. There would be a very marginal improvement in the working capital cycle

items.statement: Standalone business expected to grow a couple of percentage points faster than industry in FY25
items.quote: We believe, I think we can talk about our numbers and I think our first quarter is representative of where we see our business to be this year, a couple of percentage points maybe plus on that.

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 revenue growth expected to be lower than Q1's 28% YoY
items.quote: We believe that it will be difficult to maintain this momentum, we have quarter-on-quarter, on a full year basis. So I would probably look at a more muted number of a lower number from that level.

items.statement: New businesses expected to reach 60-65% of revenue in 3-5 years from current 43%
items.quote: We believe that the new businesses would probably have 60% to 65% of revenue going forward. Currently, it's at 43% levels, and we expect to grow to about 60% loss level.

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 capex estimated at INR55 crores, split nearly equally between businesses
items.quote: I think we are looking to have these capex plan in all our businesses put together, about INR55 odd crores in that.

items.statement: Bangalore plant balancing capex ongoing in FY25 and FY26, not substantial
items.quote: We have some balancing capex going on for this year and next financial year. It is not a dramatic capex but we have some balancing capex is going on quality measures, , but nothing, not a very substantial number.

items.statement: LCV business expected to reach 10% of total revenues by Q3/Q4 FY25, dependent on FAME policy
items.quote: By the third and fourth quarters, our expectation and hope is that LCV business should be 10% of our total revenues. But I have to say that this will depend to some part in what announcements the government makes on FAME-III or whatever other policy they come up with.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 14.8% in Q1 FY25 from 14.1% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: The margins increased from 14.1% to 14.8% in this quarter.

items.statement: MCU business steady-state EBITDA margin targeted at low double digits by FY26 or FY27
items.quote: We believe that the steady state EBITDA margin for this business will be in the low double digits. But it's not something that we'll be able to get to this year. It's probably something that we will aspire to in FY '26 or maybe even FY '27.

items.statement: No price hikes in fastener business during Q1; growth driven by volume
items.quote: No, we have not. It's all about volume growth.

items.statement: Steel prices stable with marginal softness; pass-through mechanism limits margin impact
items.quote: The softness is there, but it's not dramatic to improve -- drop in prices and even the margin on prices, the impact in the margin structure is marginal, maybe a mathematical equation is, but otherwise, there's a pass-through to the customer will come through.

items.statement: Overall auto demand muted in Q1 FY25; EV 2-wheeler sales at 182,000 units
items.quote: On the industry front, the demand for automobiles was a bit muted during Q1 at FY '25. The EV 2-wheeler industry continues to gain momentum and the cumulative sales stood at 1,82,000 units in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Festive season EV demand dependent on FAME III government policy announcement
items.quote: Look, a lot depends on what the government does with FAME, I mean, if you're talking about - - if you're talking about EV , I mean, the government's announcement of our FAME III will definitely help

items.statement: SGEM revenue share rose to 43% in Q1 FY25 from 33% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: The revenue share of SGEM in the overall business has risen from 33% in Q1 FY '24 to 43% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Added customers in 3-wheeler, LCV and entry-level electric scooter segments for Sterling Gtake
items.quote: In our Sterling Gtake business, we have added customers in the 3-wheeler and LCV space as well as a customer in the entry-level electric scooter space. So these are revenues that we expect to see kick in by the end of this year.

items.statement: High customer concentration in SGEM with top 5 customers well north of 90% of revenue
items.quote: I would say the top 5 would be a very high percentage, well north of 90%. But I've not calculated the number, but definitely about 90% because the smaller customers haven't taken off yet.

items.statement: LCV EV penetration dependent on government FAME policy announcements
items.quote: We are not still seeing traction with -- think the industry is waiting for some kind of announcements from the government on FAME, and so we should move forward.

items.statement: Management expects asset quality improvements post-Diwali and will grow disbursements only when comfortable with quality
items.quote: But if I had to venture a guess, I would say that post-Diwali, you should start seeing improvements come again.

items.statement: Yields may decline by another 25-30 bps in coming quarters but no larger decline expected
items.quote: So we don't expect yields to decline too much further, maybe by another 25, 30 bps in the coming quarters, but nothing larger than that.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance revised up by ~50 bps from previous 2.5-3% range
items.quote: Maybe by 50 bps at this point, but nothing too crazy.

items.statement: Management believes credit cost should not exceed 3.5% but cannot guarantee
items.quote: But my experience and the fact that we have somewhat stabilized on the repayment rates -- leads me to believe that it shouldn't get really worse than 3.5% or so.

items.statement: Disbursements degrew ~13% YoY in Q1 FY25 due to cautious approach prioritizing portfolio quality
items.quote: Total disbursements for the quarter stood at INR459 crores as compared to INR530 crores in the same period last year. Disbursements degrew by approximately 13 %.

items.statement: Consolidated yield 25.4%, NIM 15.5%, cost-to-income 28.7% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Consolidated yield stood at 25.4%, net interest margin stood at 15. 5% and cost to income stood at 28.7%.

items.statement: MSME disbursements grew to INR89 crores in Q1 FY25 from INR67 crores YoY with stable ticket sizes
items.quote: From Q1 to Q1 same previous year, I think it was INR67 crores and INR89 crores this quarter. So -- and even after the ticket size being pretty much the same, unchanged average ticket sizes.

items.statement: Micro LAP pilot at INR6-7 crores AUM with INR1.8 crores monthly disbursement run rate, expanding to Telangana
items.quote: As far as the portfolio is concerned, I think it's about at INR6 crores, INR7 crores right now. We have reached a run rate of almost about INR1.8 crores a month of disbursements, and that is increasing on a month-to-month basis.

items.statement: Opened 91 new branches in last 12 months, total 434 branches; piloting centralized credit managers in 100 branches by early next quarter
items.quote: In terms of branch expansion, we have opened 91 new branches over the last 12 months, bringing our total branch count to 434.

items.statement: Collection efficiency stable at 95.8% consolidated in June 2024; on-time repayment ~93.6-93.8%
items.quote: Collection efficiency for the month of 2020 -- June 2024 in our Microfinance business stood at 95.1%, MSME business stood at 97.2% and two -wheeler business stood at 96.1%. Overall, consolidated collection efficiencies stood at 95.8%.

items.statement: No significant improvement in July collections; expect stable Q2 with no major downside
items.quote: No. Unfortunately, I cannot say that there has been any improvement. So largely, things remain stable for now. And I don't think that we're going to see significant improvements in Q2, although I don't believe we'll see significant downside as well.

items.statement: Write-offs elevated due to conservative accounting; total impairment (provisions + write-offs) not expected to decline until Q3/Q4
items.quote: But as far as total impairment, whether provisioning or write -offs, I don't expect too much of a decline in the coming quarters. However, by Q3 or Q4, we should start seeing a decline.

items.statement: Over-leveraging driven by FOIR rule change, income assessment challenges, and non-MFI lenders not bound by MFI guidelines
items.quote: Now let's say, if I assess a customer at a INR2 lakh income, right, and I lever him accordingly, what is stopping another MFI from coming in and assessing the same customer at INR3 lakh income and giving him money, right?

items.statement: Implemented biometric eKYC verification across all branches using fingerprint/iris scanners to combat KYC manipulation
items.quote: And so we have successfully launched in all of our branches a biometric eKYC verification using either fingerprints or iris scanners.

items.statement: Launched Namra app for cashless payments and account info; expanding geo-tracking and BI monitoring with 25-person HO team
items.quote: We are happy to announce t hat the launch of the Namra app, which is an Android-based smartphone app, that the customers can use for as a payment gateway and also get account -related information.

items.statement: Expect tiller volumes to at least double in Q2 FY25 vs Q1 FY25
items.quote: Coming to the 2nd Quarter, we expect growth on the tiller volumes as compared to the 1st Quarter, which means we should at least double the volume over the 1st Quarter.

items.statement: Expect tractor volumes to grow 15-20% YoY in Q2 FY25
items.quote: I would not put a number, but yes, we were looking at a decent growth on last year. So, we should be looking at 15%, 20% on last year's volume.

items.statement: Expect 15%+ YoY growth for tractor segment in FY25
items.quote: Broadly, we believe that we should be definitely looking at 15%-plus growth from last year.

items.statement: Expect 15% YoY growth for tiller segment in FY25
items.quote: Yes. Tiller also we expect, yes, definitely that's the growth we are expecting in tillers also.

items.quote: Mr. Anthony had indicated that we should be looking at Rs. 2,000 crores coming from the existing products and what we are doing, that is by the years '25-'26.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve in Q2 and Q3 FY25 with top line recovery
items.quote: So, as we said that Q2 is looking better for us, so definitely margins should improve in Q2 and Q3 as well.

items.statement: July sales show recovery with 5,100 power tillers and 439 tractors sold
items.quote: So, I just captured in this slide about the sales numbers for power tiller for July, which is around 5,100 tillers and tractors are at 439.

items.statement: Good monsoon and reservoir levels driving demand recovery in Q2
items.quote: The specific reason is the monsoon has been very good. All reservoirs are almost full. Across the country, I can say, monsoon is either surplus or normal.

items.quote: And on the higher HP also we have started marketing the higher HP tractors. In the 1st Quarter we did about 40 tractors, and the network has just started coming into place.

items.statement: Export marketing for Zetor JV to start from Q3 FY25
items.quote: Exports, you're talking with exports with reference to Zetor JV? Ashish: Yes. V. T. Ravindra: Yes. No, we have not yet started marketing on the export front. That we will be looking at in probably from the third quarter onwards

items.statement: EV drivetrain supply to US autonomous tractor seeing decent orders; volumes expected better than last year
items.quote: Yes, the outlook for that is fairly good. We are seeing decent orders for that in this quarter. So, I think the volumes should be better than last year.

items.statement: In-house power weeder prototypes by Q3 FY25; commercial launch by Q4 FY25
items.quote: We have started work on the proto weeders; we are going to develop the weeders in-house. They should be out by the third quarter; we should have a couple of models for testing purposes. items.quote: I do not believe that there would be huge price savings, because right now many of the weeders that are imported are cheaper weeders that really do not last. So, we want to give a good product, and we do not want to play on the price.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic growth options for capital deployment; could be in India or globally
items.quote: We look at even some inorganic growth, which is a possibility. Right now, we cannot comment, but we are looking at some options on that

items.statement: Land monetization not imminent; board decision pending; currently used for warehousing
items.quote: It would not happen immediately. To be honest, we are at present using the setup there for our warehousing. I mean, we need to discuss this at the Board level. And there is a long-term plan, but nothing will happen in the short term.

items.statement: Monarch (EV drivetrain) revenue ~Rs 5 crore in Q1 FY25; expected to grow
items.quote: Around Rs. 5 crores is revenue from Monarch in this quarter. So, we expect this to grow in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Retail finance share for tillers at 4-5%; improving with tie-ups and loss-sharing models
items.quote: So, in terms of retail finance, if I understand the question, it's more on retail finance, so we are at roughly at same percentage which you mentioned, around 4% to 5%, but we hope this number to grow quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Target double-digit EBITDA within 2 years from now

items.statement: Backlog increased to Rs 3,917 crores as on June 30, 2024

items.statement: Received FGD order worth about 775 crores from Jaypee Nigrie and Jaypee Bina
items.quote: Your Company has received the FGD order worth about 775 crores from Jaypee Nigrie and Jaypee Bina.

items.quote: we are annualizing in terms of one or two orders that we will announce per year. And that value you can assume to be in the range of 300 to 500 crores per year.

items.quote: The same is also reflected in the performance on the loss before tax which stood at Rs. 11 crores of loss in the current quarter against loss before tax of Rs 136 crores in the corresponding quarter of previous year for the standalone entity.

items.statement: Favorable shift in sales mix with higher contribution from high margin service business

items.statement: Durgapur factory Q1 FY25 clocked about 40,000 hours

items.quote: This transaction provides about 214 crores plus 38 crores which is about 252 crores net liability reduction which will improve net worth of your Company, and this will further be boosted by consideration of gas business of 44 crores. items.statement: Working capital cycle target reduced from 10 years average to 2-3 years
items.quote: We now have a strategy for the Company which is margin accretive, cash accretive to focus in improving the working cycle capital of the Company from an average of 10 years to 7 years today to a future of an average working capital cycle of about 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Global electricity demand projected to grow ~4% in 2024 and 2025
items.quote: According to the IEA's electricity linear update, global electricity demand is anticipated to grow by approximately 4% in 2024 up from 2.5% in 2023. items.statement: Durgapur factory expanding into pressure vessels, cryogenic applications and export of parts to 13 countries
items.quote: The areas that we are currently focusing to get this load one for sure services in India. With the recent strategies of also now we will target parts to 13 more countries outside India where we will supply mills and parts fabricated in Durgapur. We see some traction there. The third area that we are working on Durgapur is the cryogenic and pressure vessels.

items.statement: FGD EP scope roughly 30% of total EPC value

items.statement: Practically impossible to complete FGD projects within current 2027 deadline; developers may order then seek extensions
items.quote: That is practically, you are right. It's practically impossible. We don't see that sense of urgency anywhere today. items.statement: Full year consolidated revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20%
items.quote: So I would say that the full year guidance for the consolidated entities could be anywhere between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth guidance around 10% for FY25
items.quote: However, as stand-alone should probably be maybe close to around 10% or so, just the stand-alone.

items.statement: Subsidiaries revenue growth guidance 30% to 35% for FY25
items.quote: Probably around 30% to 35%, is the growth we are looking at the subsidiaries.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance to sustain current levels for FY25
items.quote: And my estimate and my guidance would be that we should be able to sustain the current EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Full year capex guidance revised to INR120-140 crores from earlier INR150-175 crores
items.quote: However, with many SOP planned for the second half of the year, the capex outlay for the whole year is estimated to be around INR120 crores to INR140 crores, down by earlier guidance of INR150 crores to INR175 crores.

items.statement: Total order book INR1,000 crores with 90% new business and 40% EV contribution
items.quote: The total order book, considering the value of all four domains is INR1,000 crores, out of which 90% is new business. 25% of the total order book will mature in second half of FY '25, 55% in the next fiscal year FY '26 and the remaining 20% in FY '27. items.statement: IAC normalized EBITDA margin sustainable at 17%

items.statement: Consolidated manpower cost sustainable at 13% of sales

items.statement: Aftermarket expected to post double-digit growth for full fiscal year despite Q1 flatness

items.statement: Passenger vehicle headwinds expected to continue in Q2 with growth recovery in H2

items.quote: So corrected for that, the adj usted EBITDA stands at INR 109 crores, which is a 44% year-on-year growth and adjusted EBITDA margin would be at 6.2%, which would be a 90-basis point improvement over the previous

items.statement: Fashion fulfillment expenses reduced 167 bps YoY via air-to-land optimization and lower RTOs; marketing expenses improved 101 bps via better repeat ratio and conversion.
items.quote: Our fulfillment expenses have reduced by about 167 bps, this is a gain a concerted effort where we've been working on optimizing delivery from certain legs from air to land, faster deliveries, which has also reduced leakages, which we spoke about earlier, reduce RTO, has also reduced fulfillment expenses. So all moving again in the right direction. The marketing expenses improved by about 101 bps.

items.statement: Fashion owned brands GMV declined 14% YoY on 3P channels in Q1 FY25, partially offset by 10% growth on Nykaa Fashion platform; management calls performance disappointing but not a long-term trend.
items.quote: However, this is due to channel degrowth in 3P channels where we're degrown at 14% year -on-year. However, this is compensated by th e GMV growth and Nykaa Fashion platform where they grew 10%. Again, I think this performance is a bit disappointing. I wouldn't read into it as a long -term trend and efforts are on to increase the innovation and performance of the fashion owned brands

items.statement: Fashion 'First in Fashion' new launches contributed 24% of GMV in Q1 FY25, up from prior year, growing 37% YoY; Luxe Indian wear added 200+ brands in 6 months.
items.quote: We've seen a 37% GMV growth year-on-year of these new launches that all the brands in the country have done and its contribution to our total GMV was 24% in this quarter. Again, this is higher than it was last year. Last year, again, cementing our belief in creating newness conversation and excitement in fashion as a category.

items.statement: Beauty annual unique transacting customers grew 21% YoY to 13.1M; orders grew 26% YoY to 12.4M in Q1 FY25; new customer acquisition grew 27% YoY.
items.quote: In terms of annual unique transacting customers, this grew at 21% taking us to 13.1 million unique transacting customers for the year. And the number of orders that were placed on the platform for the quarter was about 12.4 million orders, which is a 26% growth year-over-year.

items.statement: Nykaa Play relaunch drove 35% higher cart additions and 30% higher visits per visitor for engaged users vs non-engaged users in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: And you can see that Nykaa Play's relaunch has led to a 35% higher cart addition by those who are actually actively using the Nykaa Play feature on the app versus those who are not, and also 30% higher visits per visitor of those who are actively using and engaging with Nykaa Play.

items.statement: Marketing expense for Beauty segment expected to remain range bound at 8.5% to 9.0% of sales
items.quote: I think somewhere around the 8.5% to 9.0%.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expanded 30 bps YoY in Q1 FY25; normalized expansion 90 bps excluding GCC and restructuring expenses
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded by 30 basis points during the quarter with a higher than revenue growth of 31%.

items.statement: Fashion gross margins improved 360 bps YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by higher marketing and servicing income
items.quote: Our fashion gross margins in Q1 improved by 360 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis, primarily driven by higher marketing and servicing income.

items.statement: Beauty BPC gross margins remained largely steady YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: While gross margins in BPC remained largely steady.

items.statement: Heavy lifting on warehouse expansion for express delivery largely behind; incremental last-mile fulfillment cost may come but not very meaningful
items.quote: I do believe a lot of the heavy lifting is now behind us.

items.statement: Optimistic on services income recovery in H2 FY25 driven by festive season and D2C brands returning to advertising
items.quote: So that's a positive trend, which we think should strengthen as we get into the second half of the year, which tends to be where most of the festive occasions are and a lot of the seasonal, and festive shopping for this category will occur.

items.statement: Expect discounting to moderate in H2 FY25 if demand revives during festive season
items.quote: And I think if that happens, you will see the discount ing should moderate, and that should, again, help reduce the buildup

items.statement: Owned beauty brands growing across all channels; channel mix shifts reflect Dot & Key rollout in stores and GT/MT expansion for Kay Beauty
items.quote: All the beauty on brands are growing across all the channels. It just might happen to be that, for example, others, it's coming off of a smaller base, right?

items.statement: Foot Locker e-commerce partnership launch scheduled for October 2024
items.quote: We've announced a Foot Locker Association, where we are going to represent all the Foot Locker's e-commerce demand in the country, and that launch is going to happen in October of this year.

items.statement: Acquired majority stake in Earth Rhythm; board approved increasing stake in Dot & Key to 90% and making Earth Rhythm a subsidiary
items.quote: The Board of Directors at its meeting held today has also approved acquisition of further stake in Dot & Key, which will take our stake to 90% as well as in Earth Rhythm, which will make it a subsidiary of the company.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of western wear and accessories business from Nykaa Fashion via slump sale in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Completed the acquisition of western wear and accessories business from Nykaa Fashion by a slump sale in quarter 1 FY '25.

items.statement: Fashion growth impacted by seasonality and step-function dynamics; Indian wear weakness and western wear underperformance on third-party platforms in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The quarter was tough due to two elements, mainly on third-party platform where it has been listed on Myntra few other platforms. We didn't perform as well.

items.statement: Packaging cost reduction in eB2B driven by reuse and recycling of outer packaging materials over last 6-7 quarters
items.quote: What we have been driving for last, I think, 6-7 quarters is that a lot of our outer packaging, we are reusing recycling materials for the brand boxes.

items.statement: No incremental guidance provided; management cautions against reading too much into quarterly margin fluctuations
items.quote: I would just like to caution that, yes, Fashion gross profit margin looked very good, but there are quarter-on-quarter differences. And I would say that some of it is definitely noncore.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain ~20% growth at least till H1 FY25; internal targets split between H1 and H2 with high hopes for Diwali
items.quote: We've still been able to post a 20% growth. So, I think we will try and maintain this at least till H1. Once the market conditions improve, things start happening, then probably internally also we're looking at H1 separately, and then we're looking at H2.

items.statement: Total FY25 capex ~Rs 30 cr for hard luggage plant plus Rs 5-6 cr for warehousing phase 1 plus regular store capex
items.quote: overall project was about ₹30 odd crores, and we're deploying that. Apart from that, there's some CapEx that we are also deploying towards our warehousing that will also entail about anywhere between ₹5 crores to ₹6 crores of CapEx.

items.statement: Juicy Couture license signed for 10+5 years with lower royalty; women handbags expected to reach 15-20% of portfolio in next couple of years
items.quote: the contract is 10 plus five. So, we get a 15 -year license ideally. 10 years is the contract period, and there's an auto renewal clause of another five years. So, we get a long-term contract. And the royalty percentage is also quite lucrative.

items.statement: Margins improved sequentially from Q4 but remain below year-ago quarter due to subdued same-store sales, higher royalty on old inventory, and pre-operative expenses; expects recovery in coming quarters if market improves
items.quote: The margins have been improved from Q4, of course, the last preceding quarter, but still subdued from the previous same year quarter. The reasons remain to be the same as I had explained even during my last call that a same -store sales, the growth has been subdued.

items.statement: Adding Juicy Couture as super premium bridge-to-luxury women's handbag/accessories brand; also exploring marketplace model on bagline.com for curated premium brands; UCB small leather goods now #2 at Shoppers Stop
items.quote: Juicy Couture is a very, very, strategic addition to our portfolio. We've been eyeing this space, where we look at our women handbag kind of a brand. And the price point is going to be more in the super premium bridge to luxury kind of a category

items.statement: Bangladesh unrest impacting competitors who source heavily from there; management sees this as positive for Brand Concepts
items.quote: all the big-ticket players were sourcing a lot from Bangladesh. Yeah, there is going to be an impact for them. Good for us.

items.statement: IFF merger in NCLT; shareholders meeting end of September, completion expected by end of Q3 FY25; operational integration already underway with new client wins
items.quote: IFF, I think we are already in NCLT. And if I'm not mistaken, towards the end of September is when the Shareholders Meeting is supposed to happen. And I think after that, it'll take another couple of months , so four months max.

items.statement: CSD channel showing brilliant sell-through in limited depots; margins currently lower due to locked-in pre-COVID pricing but price escalation allowed after one year; focus now on expanding points of sale
items.quote: The traction is very good actually. The sell through is very good. Sales are in whatever limited number of th is thing that canteen that we've gone, we've seen a brilliant response over there. So, now is the time when we geared up, and we will sort of start expanding on that entire segment.

items.statement: Vertical brand experimenting in mass-market luggage distribution with good initial response; leveraging upcoming in-house manufacturing for pricing power; Sugarush confined to EBOs
items.quote: We've experimented with two models in Vertical in distribution space, in MBO space. And we've taken a very, very different sort of route, very different strategy. And I'm happy to share that the markets have responded pretty well, very good, actually to those strategies.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target 10-12%; management prefers reinvesting profits for growth over margin maximization; aims to scale from ~Rs 70 cr quarterly run-rate toward Rs 2,000-3,000 cr potential
items.quote: I believe there are 12%, 13% , anything between 10 % to 12% of an EBITDA is a good EBITDA, right? It's a decent EBITDA. We're not very extremely good, but we're not extremely bad also. Let's maintain that and then plough back that whole money to grow.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected in late teens for FY25
items.quote: I think, Damayanti just to anticipate that , our growth (Revenue) probably for this year will be kind of late teens.

items.statement: Matured hospitals revenue growth expected to reach double digits in coming quarters
items.quote: Typically, the quarter first remains very muted. Still, we could show gro wth of 7.3% year -on- year basis and as we enter into the season which is September and December, you'll see more healthy growth in the double digits going forward

items.statement: Invested INR 56.7 crores in capex during Q1 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, the company invested roughly INR56.7 crores in ongoing capital expenditures.

items.statement: Gurugram flagship hospital capex per bed around INR 1.5 crores
items.quote: I think it will be around 1.5 Cr. Yes, for sure.

items.statement: Rajahmundry and Hennur Bangalore hospitals expected to commence operations in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Both are expected to commence operations in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Coimbatore regional hub hospital project started, expected completion in 24 months
items.quote: The project work for the regional hub hospital in Coimbatore (~ 130 beds) has just started and is expected to complete in 24 months' time.

items.statement: Matured hospitals EBITDA margin slightly improved year-on-year, no erosion
items.quote: We are not seeing any margin erosion. In fact, in the matured hospitals they operate on the operating leverage. So any incremental revenue growth will always improve the EBITDA or EBITDA margins.

items.statement: New hospitals cost structure 90-95% settled, minimal incremental cost expected
items.quote: more or less I think 90%-95% the cost is settled there. As we grow these units and new clinical teams join, there may be some impact but not major

items.statement: Hydernagar, Himayat Nagar, Sarjapura hospitals to achieve EBITDA breakeven by end of FY25, Chennai by H1 FY26
items.quote: So then potentially the Hydernagar, Himayat Nagar and the Sarjapura Hospital should achieve EBITDA break even by end of this year. And Chennai, you are possibly targeting break even in first half of next year.

items.statement: Three new hospitals commissioned in Q4 FY24 adding 280 beds, total capacity over 2,000 beds
items.quote: In the last quarter, we marked a significant milestone by commissioning three new hospitals, one each in Hyderabad, Bangalore and Chennai, adding a total of 280 beds. This brings our total capacity to over 2,000 beds, including managed beds in New Delhi.

items.statement: Outpatient footfalls, inpatient admissions and deliveries showing significant improvement
items.quote: Our outpatient footfalls, inpatient admissions and deliveries are all showing significant improvement.

items.statement: IVF program expanded to 11 units with impressive organic footfalls
items.quote: Now we've got to about 11 total. Now I think all of them are commissioned, all the embryology services have started, the doctors have been recruited, the business plan is laid out. And I think whatever the early footfalls that we are seeing are pretty impres sive and are pretty organic

items.statement: New hospitals priced attractively initially, insurance tie-ups take 6-9 months to settle
items.quote: One is that you want to be attractive for the patients. Generally, in a new hospital, people see how expensive it is. First thing is you don't want to get that in major name. So, you will definitely price it attractively in the beginning.

items.statement: Gurugram project may face 4-6 month delay due to government approval processes
items.quote: I think there may be a four to six months delay because we didn't expect that it will take about a year to get the land parcels registered and now we applied for the permissions.

items.statement: New hospitals breakeven at ~35% occupancy, Hyderabad within 12 months, Bangalore 12-15 months, Chennai 15-18 months
items.quote: Usually about 35% occupancy we break even. And a t a place like Bangalore, it will take about 12 to 15 months time. Chennai might take about 15 to 18 months

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 518 crores as of June 30, 2024, sufficient to fund all planned capex without debt
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with a net cash position of INR518 crores as of June 30, 2024 which will support our ongoing capital expenditure plans. Given our current cash flow and anticipated internal accruals in the coming years, we are confident in our ability to complete all planned capital expenditures through internal accruals without acquiring debt financing.

items.statement: Topline growth guidance of 18-20% for FY25 maintained; bottom line growth now expected at 15-18% due to duty cut impact
items.quote: we are confident that we will achieve overall 18% to 20% growth throughout the year subject to quarterly variances.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 at 7-8%; gross margin guidance at 14-15%
items.quote: We have said 14% 14.5% to 15% and EBITDA we have said 7 % to 8%.

items.statement: Plan to open 18-20 stores in FY25; 6 stores opened in Q1 (4 COCO, 2 franchisee, 1 in Dubai)
items.quote: we have been planning and aiming to open about 18 to 20 stores for the whole financial year and in Q1 we have opened six stores out of the 18 to 20 stores

items.statement: Q1 gross margin expanded ~500bps YoY due to better business quality, franchisee pricing tweaks, and rising gold price benefit on making charges
items.quote: gross margin has also been in a good range, primarily because what we see is that subsequent to the earlier quarters, like last year's Q1, or Q1 FY 22-23, we've seen an improvement in the quality of our business.

items.statement: Customs duty cut (9%) creates ~Rs 50 crore inventory loss on gold loan portion; impact spread over Q2-Q3
items.quote: we are analysing and assuming that approximately 50 crores of financial impact would be there due to the duty that has already been paid and the market value that has been coming down.

items.statement: Post duty cut (last 15-20 days), footfalls and sales up sharply; Q2 YTD growth ~25-30% implying 18-20% YTD
items.quote: growth number as on date can be assumed to be at 18% to 20

items.statement: Studded ratio fell to 9.6-9.7% in Q1 (vs 11.5% FY24); target 12-13% for FY25 via inventory build and attractive pricing
items.quote: our target remains the same. It is only one or two quarters, as you said, do not decide the journey. The journey very clearly remains a confident journey. And more so, since our diamond prices are quite attractive, we are with the competition. We are sure that we will achieve the 12.5% to 13% this year. But surely, we will touch 12%.

items.statement: Gold metal loan portion (~40-45% of hedging) unhedged to duty changes; further duty cuts would hurt
items.quote: But we need to keep in mind that GML will not have an impact of that, if there is any further duty cut, then GML will not be the right way to hedge.

items.statement: Hedging at ~95% in Q1 (MCX ~50-55%, Gold Metal Loan ~40-45%); gold loan portion exposed to duty changes
items.quote: hedging percentage has been, we said in the press release also, has been ~95%.

items.statement: Gold exchange rising due to higher gold prices and trust shift from unorganised to organised; target 40-45% of sales
items.quote: Higher gold exchange clearly is for two reasons. One is the increasing gold price and which is a major reason the customer has to buy gold he doesn't have money and he brings the old gold. Secondly, the trust and movement from unorganized to organized in the respective market.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond pilot in 3-4 stores; not yet breakeven; FY25 revenue contribution Rs 50-100 crore
items.quote: in the current year, in 24-25, when we talk about the Sennes segment, which consists of lab-grown perfume and the leather bags, the contribution is not likely to be more than Rs 100 crores. I have said earlier Rs 50 crores. I think between Rs 50 crores to Rs 100 crores.

items.statement: International expansion calibrated; first store in Dubai opened; focus on brand building before scaling
items.quote: we will be in a very methodical and a calibrated manner doing our expansion abroad.

items.statement: FY28 revenue aspiration of Rs 2000 crore if roads and building segments expand
items.quote: And if we increase the building a little and increase the road, if we go to the highway, then it will be 2000 plus, very easily.

items.statement: Order book stands at over Rs 1800 crore unexecuted work
items.quote: Sir, in excess of 1800 crores unexecuted work is with us.

items.statement: Bid pipeline exceeds Rs 4000 crore with 10-15% expected conversion rate
items.quote: The bid pipeline is more than Rs. 4000 crores, where we have participated and the maximum result should be within one to two months.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 24-26% considered sustainable across water, road HAM and building projects
items.quote: Yes, sir, these are all projects with the same margins.

items.statement: Significant increase in water sector works expected from government entities post-budget
items.quote: I think there's going to be a significant increase in the water sector works that are going to come out of the government entities.

items.statement: Order book split 75% water segment, 25% other segments
items.quote: 75% water segment, 25% from other.

items.statement: Acquired manufacturing property in Fatehpur, UP for Rs 50-60 crore to use as bank collateral for BG facilities
items.quote: We have acquired a manufacturing entity in Fatehpur, UP. We have told in our board meeting that our plan is to shut down by December. Ultimately, we will use that property as collateral which we need for banking facilities.

items.statement: No payment delay issues anticipated; projects funded by World Bank, ADB or central government
items.quote: We are not facing any payment delay issues. The nature of the business is such that we almost 10% to 15% of the amount gets withheld by the department in shape of retention money that is released after commissioning of the project.

items.statement: H1 revenue expected at 30-40% of annual, H2 at 60-70% due to seasonality
items.quote: So I think it would be anywhere around for H1 it would be based on year-to-year 30% to 40% and for H2 it would be 60% to 70%.

items.statement: No fundraising requirement currently; working capital sufficient for project execution
items.quote: Now the requirement is not there. It depends on how many project gets converted, it is based on that too, but as of now there is no requirement. We have working capital available and we can do in that.

items.statement: Cash realization of Rs 125-150 crore from trade receivables in Q1 FY25
items.quote: It will be around Rs. 125-150 crores.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15-17% for FY25
items.quote: Last year also we had a revenue growth of 15% to 17%, which would be in overall lines. This year, in terms of revenue growth, Q1, we are around 6% in terms of the passenger vehicle segment and about 14% in commercial vehicle segment. Going forward, Q2, Q3, Q4, and the larger numbers coming from these three quarters, we would be at an overall of about 15% to 17% overall growth.

items.statement: Service business revenue growth target of 20-25% for FY25
items.quote: Service business, we target to grow by approximately 20% to 25%, and that will be the guidance for the year also.

items.statement: Q2 expected to cover Q1 volume shortfall with festival season starting August 17
items.quote: We are confident that Q2 will cover up the shortfall of Q1 in terms of volume sales.

items.statement: EV two-wheeler sales expected to recover from August with Ather Rizta launch
items.quote: We are expecting the sales, the amount of booking, the number of bookings that we have is quite considerable. And we are expecting sales as soon as supplies happen, starting from August through the next three quarters to be very robust.

items.statement: EBITDA margin depressed at 4% in Q1 due to weak service business from climatic conditions
items.quote: Service being a main driver of EBITDA margin, these conditions led to a depressed margin in this quarter. EBITDA reduced by approximately 3% compared to last year.

items.statement: Average selling price increased across new vehicles, pre-owned, and service segments
items.quote: We have seen an uptrend in our average selling price, increased from INR 8,54,057 to INR 9,62,403.

items.statement: EV investments negligible at ~INR 1.5 crores for Piaggio across seven centres
items.quote: We have made approximately just about INR 1.5 crores of investments in Piaggio across seven centres per se.

items.statement: Credit rating upgrades for two subsidiaries: Popular Auto Works BBB- to BBB+, Prabal Motors BBB to A-
items.quote: two of our subsidi aries, one is Popular Auto Works Private Limited, got double notch credit rating upgradation from BBB - to BBB+. Whereas the other subsidiar y, Prabal Motors Private Limited, also got a double notch rating upgradation from BBB to A

items.statement: Revenue mix: PV 5.4% growth, CV 14% growth, EV -39.5% decline in Q1
items.quote: PV revenue .i.e., passenger vehicles revenue was INR 734 crores versus INR 696 crores in Q1 FY '24, which is an increase of about 5.4% year-on-year. Commercial vehicle was INR 479.9 crores versus INR 420.8 crores in Q1 FY '24, an increase of 14% Y-o-Y. EV revenue was INR 13.6 crores versus INR 22.4 crores in Q1 FY '24, a decrease of 39.5% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Bookings nearly double July daily average in last 4-5 days ahead of Onam festival
items.quote: In the last four-five days, we are seeing that the bookings are almost double of what has been the July daily average.

items.statement: Appointed Chief Risk Officer effective August 13
items.quote: We are pleased t o announce the appointment of our Chief Risk Officer with effect from 13th August, that is yesterday. So Jarly, who is the Head Finance of our Pop ular Vehicles and Services division, has been given the additional responsibility of CRO

items.statement: Adding seven new service centers in FY25 after adding seven in FY24
items.quote: Last year we have built about seven new service centers. And I mean, like I said, this year too, we have another seven centers coming up.

items.statement: Honda ASP grew 12% in Q1; revenue grew 8% despite only 2% volume growth
items.quote: In fact, Honda ASP has gone up by 12%. So overall the revenue of Honda actually grew up by 8% in Q1 compared to previous year.

items.statement: Annual EBITDA margin guidance of around 18% and PAT margin of 11-12%
items.quote: In the past also, we have given a guidance of 18% EBITDA and around 11% to 12% of PAT. And that's how historically our margin profile has been.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 25-30% year-on-year for next couple of years
items.quote: From the revenue perspective, we are definitely looking at around 25 to 30% increase year on year. That is what has happened in the last year as well. And we should be able to exceed that in the next couple of years as well.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs. 12,461 million with 91% domestic, 9% international; 95% heating equipment, 5% waste gas handling
items.quote: Our order book remains strong, standing at Rs. 12,461 million with a well-diversified composition. Geographically, 91% of our current order book is driven by the Indian customer requirement and 9% orders coming from the international markets.

items.statement: Complete Rs. 1,246 crore order book should ideally get executed in FY25 and FY26
items.quote: So, just to answer your question in short, the complete Rs. 1,246 crores order book should ideally get executed in this year and next year.

items.statement: Bid pipeline roughly Rs. 4,000 crore with Rs. 1,000-1,500 crore domestic and Rs. 2,000-2,500 crore export opportunities
items.quote: So, basically, the bid pipeline roughly stands at something like Rs. 4,000 crore, wherein maybe about Rs. 1,000-1,500 crores is for domestic and Rs. 2,000-2,500 crores is for exports.

items.statement: Expect order inflow to be better in FY26 vs FY25 considering announced projects in India and abroad
items.quote: It is a bit difficult to comment on that as of now. But, yes, generally it looks like that considering the projects announced in India and also the projects expected abroad. It looks like that. The inflow should be better in FY26 vs 25, yes.

items.statement: No additional capex needed for Reliance cracking furnace order; existing facilities sufficient
items.quote: And we don't need any additional capex to execute this project. Whatever the existing facilities we have, that is sufficient. We might have to create some facilities at the site to execute the job.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 13.4% down from prior year due to lower quarterly revenue, ESOP provision of Rs. 54.6 million, and revenue mix
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has gone down as compared to the same period last year. This is mainly due to the increased operational cost as we scale up our business and invest in future growth. Also, the creation of ESOP reserves to the tune of Rs. 54.6 million for the employee benefit.

items.statement: ESOP provision of Rs. 5.46 crore made in Q1; similar provisions expected each quarter in FY25 depending on share price
items.quote: Yes, Sagar, this provision is made for this quarter and every quarter there will be a provision, and that provision corresponds to the market value at the end of the quarter.

items.statement: No price escalation clauses; raw material ~10% of order value; critical materials procured immediately or back-to-back to hedge fluctuations
items.quote: Generally, we do not have the price escalation clause in the purchase orders, but what happens is that the raw material purchased by us from a percentage perspective is quite low. It is, not even maybe 10% of the order value.

items.statement: Export project finalizations delayed but expecting closures in FY25; CPCL project may spill to FY26
items.quote: Yes, there has been a bit of a delay in terms of the finalization on the export project which we have quoted. So, the big pipeline stands as it is. So, we are definitely expecting certain closure in this fiscal, no doubt about it, it did get delayed.

items.statement: Historical revenue execution: ~1/3 in H1, ~2/3 in H2; Q3 and Q4 roughly double Q1 and Q2
items.quote: Historically, what has been the case is whatever we had done in Q1 and Q2, almost double we have done in Q3 and Q4. That has been the historical trend.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs. 300 crores primary capital strengthening balance sheet for working capital and growth
items.quote: The past year has been particularly noteworthy for us, culminating in our IPO which has raised Rs. 300 crores in primary capital. So, this IPO marks a new chapter for JNK India, providing the capital required for our support to grow future ambitions.

items.statement: Targeting Rs 900-1,000 crores top line in next 3-4 years with parallel bottom line growth
items.quote: That's the target. That's a very clear target, primarily. And more than the top line also, we are focused on making sure that we're able to get our bottom line also growing parallelly.

items.statement: Planning 11 new stores across three formats in FY25, targeting 100 stores in 3-4 years
items.quote: We are planning 11 stores this financial year. We are more or less on track for that. Having said that, we are not one of those companies who want to rush into store opening because real estate plays a very important role in our business and finding the suitable real estate still remains a very big challenge.

items.statement: Gross margin dropped to 53.2% in Q1 from 56.5% in Q4 due to sea freight costs, airlifting leather, forex impact and bulk sale at lower margin
items.quote: On gross margin, Q4, gross margins were 56.5% and current Q1 is about 53.2%. What really impacted was because of sea shipment, which is we import leather from sea, because of the sea freight going up and also the delays in arrivals of these shipments, we had to airlift a lot of leather or a lot of imported goods for our supply chain.

items.statement: Expect gross margin to recover to 56% range from Q2 onwards through price hike, shipment cost stabilization, localization and operating efficiency
items.quote: What we believe is from Q2 onwards, we should come back to our 56% range I mean, you know, like all the scenarios and those one-time bulk sale that we had in Q1. Without that, we should go back broadly to our Q4 margins.

items.statement: Leather localization at 30-33% currently, targeting 75% in 18-24 months for 20-22% overall cost savings
items.quote: Currently, around 30 %, 33% of our leather has been localized. My target is to get to a point of 75% localization in the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Expect solid housing delivery to start H2 FY25 with 30,000 units sold above Rs 3 cr in past 4 years, 85% delayed
items.quote: We are expecting solid delivery to start happening perhaps by H2. And most of the projects that were delayed are now coming almost into completion stage. And we expect a very good housing handover to happen in H2, starting from H2 of this year.

items.statement: KCD (kitchen) pilot in Bangalore executed 100 projects, planning gradual pan-India rollout over 1.5 years
items.quote: While we have successfully launched our KCD in Bangalore only Bangalore last year in September and we have done the pilot marketing here, we are happy to say that we have taken close to about 150 projects and executed close to 100 projects in Bangalore.

items.statement: Took small price hike to offset cost pressures, plus shipment cost stabilizing and localization benefits

items.quote: Point number one, you will notice we are taking a lot of hospital projects which are not in a prime location in terms of a big city. What happens is these projects are generally not in the radar of politicians. The fund is allocated by the departments in their health care projects, there is very little risk of them being stalled or cancelled if there is any political change in the state.

items.statement: Net debt risen to Rs 38 Crores due to real estate JV investments; CRISIL BBB+/A2 stable rating; short-term bridge debt of ~Rs 40 Crores for project launches
items.quote: The status of debt. This fiscal year, we have seen our total debt go up because we are involved in new real estate joint ventures. As a result, our net debt has risen to Rs 38 Crores over the past last year. Even with this increase, we are committed to capital financial management and are focused on sustainable growth and creating value.

items.statement: GMP Q1 FY25 revenue Rs 79 Crores (42% YoY), gross margin 26%, EBITDA Rs 4 Crores (6% margin)
items.quote: GMP continues to deliver improved performance during the quarter. Revenue of Rs 79 Crores in Q1 FY '25, which is up 42% year-on-year and a healthy gross margin of 26%. The EBITDA was Rs 4 Crores with a 6% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Real estate Q1 FY25 sales booking 12,244 sq ft, Rs 7 Crores sale value, Rs 11 Crores collections
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, we achieved new sales booking totalling 12,244 Square Feet, generating a sale value of Rs 7 Crores and a total collection of Rs 11 Crores.

items.statement: TEU volumes grew 13% quarter-on-quarter and close to 80% year-on-year in Q1 FY25, reaching around 17,186 TEUs.
items.quote: If you look at the TEU numbers, the volumes have been seeing a steady growth in past quarters and if you look at the Q2 of FY24, so we've we started at 12,460 and now we've been consistently growing and now in the Q1 FY25, the numbers are close to around 17,186.

items.statement: Air freight volumes grew 60% quarter-on-quarter in Q1 FY25, supported by IATA accreditation received last year.

items.statement: Revenue was ₹102.8 crores in Q1 FY25, up 9.1% quarter-on-quarter and 2.4 times year-on-year.
items.quote: I think the overall top line has improved quite a lot in this quarter. we closed at ₹102.8 crores overall and which we've seen a 9.1% increase on quarter to quarter and almost 2.4 times increase year on year.

items.statement: EBITDA increased 10.6% quarter-on-quarter and nearly doubled year-on-year in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has also increased on quarter-to-quarter basis. EBITDA has increased by 10.6% and almost two times what it was year on year.

items.statement: Management expects growth to continue in the current and coming quarters due to a good pipeline and tailwinds.
items.quote: Overall, we feel that's the reason even the PAT margins have been better. So overall, we are seeing that the company has done well in last quarter and this growth is going to continue in this quarter and coming quarter as well because the pipeline is good.

items.statement: Management does not see major challenges in coming quarters and is focused on strengthening position beyond automobiles into electronics, solar, ceramics, and commodities.
items.quote: We are not seeing any major challenges in coming quarters. items.statement: Cash reserves are being deployed for LCL acquisition targets mandated to consultancies over the last 1.5 years to fuel inorganic growth, with potential working capital needs as business grows.
items.quote: So, we are looking at some acquisition options that we've already mandated this to few companies, few consultancies where we are looking at LCL acquisition which we've been working on for last one and a half year which will fuel our inorganic growth.

items.statement: Management does not rely on disruptions like the Red Sea crisis or container shortages for growth, preferring a stable environment and long-term client acquisition in growing Indian sectors.
items.quote: We are not looking at any disruption to fuel our growth very, very clear. We are not because that all those disruptions are temporary. So, we are not looking at any disruption to help us grow. We want a stable environment because that is the long sustaining way of working.

items.statement: Freight Jar 2.0 is gaining customer traction, particularly in electronics, renewable energy, and solar sectors, serving as an entry vertical for new client acquisition.
items.quote: So, Freigsht Jar 2.0 has already been implemented where we are seeing a good traction of customers, which is happening. So that is going to continue with us because Freight Jar, the parent company is Tiger Logistics only.

items.statement: Automobile sector remains the main vertical with strong growth in 2-wheeler auto exports; focus continues on deep-selling existing clients and acquiring new ones.
items.quote: So, what has happened is that we are working very closely with developing and deep selling with our present customers, but are also looking at acquiring new customers, which is a regular process. So, the overall business, I would say has improved for auto sector also, where the auto exports is doing very well especially in the 2-Wheeler Auto sector market.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin is improving each quarter through cost and buying improvements; no specific target provided.
items.quote: Sustainable EBITDA Margin, I would say we are improving each quarter and that is the whole idea. We are working towards it trying to improve our cost overall and trying to improve our buying's overall so that is how it works.

items.statement: No major structural changes seen in the ocean freight industry; disruptions create unhealthy competition and contract dishonoring, which are not welcomed.
items.quote: No, we are not. See, of course those they made huge money after COVID. Then you know the rate drops below the COVID level pre COVID levels. They went down below that also. So, we are not seeing any major structural changes in our industry.

items.statement: Anjar facility expected to improve margins through logistics savings, automation efficiency, and fixed cost absorption, visible from Q3-Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, these all three things will add to our margin profile, and it will be properly seen once we come down to third and fourth quarter.

items.quote: So, in a month's time, we will make sure to give you a good guidance in this respect

items.statement: Expect strong top-line and bottom-line growth in near-medium term driven by strong order book outlook and customer capex cycles
items.quote: With a strong order book outlook, coupled with our strategy to capitalize on the increasing capex by our customer segments, we expect strong top-line as well as bottom-line growth in near-medium term.

items.quote: The overall capex to be spent in FY '25 would be approximately INR570 crores. This includes VOPL.

items.quote: I think one can expect normalized EBITDA margins of 26% to 27% on a sustainable basis.
