items.statement: Current debt Rs 90 crore (Rs 15 crore long-term), may add Rs 10-15 crore long-term debt for capex
items.quote: At this point of time, we have roughly Rs. 90 crore of debt in our balance sheet. About Rs. 15 crore is long term debt, and the balance is working capital. We may take an additional Rs. 10 crore - Rs. 15 crore of long-term debt going forward to complete all the CAPEX that we have planned over this year and the next year.

items.statement: S&D spend at 28-30% of revenue for last 3-4 years, working to reduce it
items.quote: Basically we are at below 30% in the S&D trends and basically if you see from last 3-4 financial years, we are between 28% and 30%. Kavita: Any outlook for the future, sir? Hemant Arora: We continue to do efforts regarding the reduction of S&D spend and we will follow the same and employ different strategies to reduce our S&D

items.statement: Can segment gross margins slightly better than bottles due to lower packaging cost
items.value: a couple of percentage points better
items.quote: On a gross margin level, it is fairly consistent with bottles as well, slightly better. You can say a couple of percentage points due to the lower packaging cost which is there in Cans.

items.statement: HoReCa channel split 25% of revenue, growing from retail-heavy 75-25 mix
items.quote: Currently as of last year, the split is roughly 75-25 with 75% coming from retail and 25% coming from HoReCa.

items.statement: Trading business revenue ~Rs 100 crore in Q1 FY25, will reduce dramatically in Q2 and shut down in Q3
items.quote: While in Q1, the trading business of the listed entity contributed approximately Rs. 100 crore in reve nue, t his will reduce dramatically in Q2 and will completely shut down in Q3

items.statement: Kolkata plant for pulses and grains to be commissioned in February 2025
items.quote: we plan to commercialize our new plant in Kolkata, dedicated to pulses and grains. Within, I think, it will be commissioned in the month of Feb 25.

items.statement: Surat plant land acquired, commissioning expected next financial year
items.quote: Additionally, we are also trying to launch a new plant in Surat, for which we have already acquired land and it will be commissioned in the next financial year.

items.statement: Edible oil refining operating margin targeted at 2% to 2.5% on processing only
items.quote: our operating margin will be around 2% to 2.5%. We will be just trying to have that on processing thing only.

items.statement: Processing margins expected to increase profit by 1.5% to 2% of revenue once plants operational
items.quote: we think our profit may increase like 1.5%, 2% of the revenue. It may increase.

items.statement: Shift from exports to domestic market focus; exports were 22% of revenue in Q1 FY24
items.quote: reducing our Reliance on exports, which accounted for approximately 22% of our revenue in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Domestic demand for food grains and pulses increasing enormously
items.quote: our domestic demands have increased very much enormously. You can say like, yes, our domestic demands have increased very much.

items.statement: Government not encouraging agri-commodity exports; focusing on ethanol production from grains
items.quote: government is not encouraging the exports of agri-commodities. They are rather planning to convert the additional grain into ethanol so that they can save on foreign exchange on import of crude oil and all.

items.statement: Kolkata plant capacity 100,000 tons per year Masoor; edible oil capacity 50,000 tons per year
items.value: 100,000 tons per year of Masoor. And around, edible is around 50,000 tons per year
items.quote: Like we are already trying to install, we are installing 100,000 tons per year of Masoor. And around, edible is around 50,000 tons per year.

items.statement: Surat plant to process lentils, channa, and matar for domestic wholesale and retail
items.quote: We are putting for pulses. Like we can process three types of pulses in that unit. One is lentils. One is channa. And the third one will be matar.

items.statement: Plan to establish brand and expand retail presence over next two to three years
items.quote: once this plant is commissioned, our focus will also be there to establish our brand. So, we are going to register our brand and we will start marketing.

items.statement: Will continue export business if government provides quotas; not exiting sugar/rice exports
items.quote: We are not going to shut down our old business. We are not going to go away from that business because that is already there. That is already established. So, we are not going to switch off anything which we are having. Rather, we will be waiting for the opportunities.

items.statement: Future plan to add one more processing unit at Bombay after current two plants
items.quote: We plan to increase our processing units. One, after this two commissioning, we'll be planning to have one more unit at Bombay.

items.statement: Management will stay with previous guidance; Q1 on track and confident of market tailwinds to cover any minor deficit
items.quote: I think we will stay with the guidance we provided last time. There is nothing that requires a review at this stage.

items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA margin is a two-year journey, not expected in FY25 due to ahead-of-curve investments in brands, people and marketing
items.quote: No, I think the guidance I have been presenting, the double digit is about a two-year journey. And so, it was not for this year.

items.statement: Chennai AAC block plant commissioning in H2 FY25 adding 2 lakh tons in first wave with capacity for another 2 lakh tons; targeting India's largest single-location plant
items.quote: The Chennai plant that will get commissione d in the second half of this year, we are adding 2 lakh tons in the first wave of that expansion, and we have capacity for another 2 lakh tons after that, which can be quickly switched

items.statement: Pipes & Fittings capacity expansion on drawing board to reach Rs 1,500 crore revenue milestone; current capacity sufficient for Rs 800-1,000 crore
items.quote: We are already on the drawing board to plan for those capacity expansion. So, yes, getting to our final eventual goal, we will need to invest more on capacity.

items.statement: Parador order bookings remain strong; third straight quarter of positive momentum on billings and order bookings
items.quote: Despite ongoing market sluggishness, Parador's order bookings remain strong. We have also introduced several new products ac ross categories to capture a larger market share

items.statement: Contribution margins improved across most segments despite price realization drops: Blocks +220 bps, Boards +170 bps, Putty +90 bps, Construction Chemicals +1,000+ bps, Parador +370 bps YoY
items.quote: In Blocks, we improved our contribution margin by 220 basis points, in Boards by 170 basis points, in Putty by 90 basis points, in Construction Chemicals by over 1,000 basis points. And at Parador, the contribution margin improved by 370 basis points.

items.statement: Price realizations fell across categories: Pipes & Fittings -12%, Putty -6%, Parador -5.7%, Blocks -3%, Panels -3.5% YoY due to aggressive competitor pricing and sluggish demand
items.quote: In Blocks, the price realization dropped by about 3%, for Panels by about 3.5%, in Putty by nearly 6%, in P ipes and Fittings by about 12%, and in Parador by about 5.7

items.statement: Q2 demand expected moderate in India with pricing challenges continuing; bounce back from September driven by government infrastructure and housing spend
items.quote: Looking ahead in Quarter 2, we expect the demand scenario to be moderate in India and challenges on pricing to continue. However, we expect a bounce back from September onwards driven by government spends on infrastructure and housing.

items.statement: B2G/JJM pipe sales at only 30% of normal in Q1 due to elections; budget allocation up ~50% to Rs 75,000 crore; expect normal service from September
items.quote: Overall, what we estimate is, and Ajay, you can help me, I think from steady state, the revenue was only about 30% of normal. So, the erosion was to the extent of 70%.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted ~5% away from Roofing strategically; Pipes & Fittings crossed Rs 150 cr quarterly revenue for first time (78% YoY growth); Construction Chemicals grew 35% YoY
items.quote: Significantly, in this quarter, we at HIL have made a nearly 5% swing away from Roofing in our overall revenue mix. It's a metric that we had highlighted we want to strategically shift.

items.statement: PVC price declining trend since July creates headwind for Pipes & Fittings in Q2; Parador faces transient product/channel mix pressure and one-time wage provision impacting Q1 EBITDA
items.quote: However, we need to watch out for headwinds being created by the declining trend in PVC prices since July.

items.statement: Parador EBITDA positive guidance for FY25 maintained; contribution margin +370 bps, EBITDA margin +170 bps YoY despite strategic investments in teams and marketing
items.quote: At the EBITDA level, there is also an i mprovement of nearly 170 basis points. The delta that you see is essentially because we are investing in the teams

items.statement: Blocks business targets 500-600 bps margin improvement via material cost (increasing pond ash), conversion cost and logistics; already delivered 220 bps contribution margin gain in Q1
items.quote: Having said that, in our blocks business, we believe there is an opportunity for us to improve the marg ins by nearly 500 to 600 basis points

items.statement: FY25 production target of 20 lakh tons plus, representing 14-15% growth over FY24
items.quote: This year we are targeting a growth of around 14%-15% over the last year.

items.statement: FY30 production target of 3.5 million tons, increasing market share from 20-21% to 32%
items.quote: By the year 2030 when country is requiring around 11 billion tons of manganese ore, we have targeted that we would be contributing to the tune of 32% of requirement of country which is right now around 20%-21%.

items.statement: FY25 capex target of INR 328 crores, FY26 capex target of INR 340 crores
items.quote: For last 2 years, capex is, or maybe 3 years, capex is more than our profit after tax. And even this year we have planned INR 328 crores, next year INR 340 crores.

items.statement: Capex of INR 316 crore in FY24, exceeding profit after tax
items.quote: Capex, that is capital expenditure of INR316 crore was done, which is more than profit after tax of the year.

items.statement: Environmental clearance of 24.88 lakh tons as of April 2024, targeting 10 lakh tons additional EC applications in FY25 and 10-15 lakh tons in FY26
items.quote: Look, the beginning of this year that is 1st of April 2024, we had an EC of nearly 24.88 lakh tons. And for this year, financial year 2024-2025, we have planned to apply for nearly 10 lakh tons.

items.statement: Targeting 6-7% year-on-year reduction in production cost per ton through volume growth with same manpower
items.quote: Exactly, you cannot say target, but definitely as we are targeting a growth of around 14%, 15% every year, so you can presume that reduction in cost by 6%, 7% every, on year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 blended realisation growth of 13-14% despite 30% announced price hikes due to grade mix
items.quote: No, what you see, I mean, it is just one or two grades. But we have a lot many grades, so it is a mix of that. Which grade is having how much demand and how much could be dispatched.

items.statement: Q2 prices likely to continue at current levels, Q3 onwards prices will decline following regular seasonal pattern
items.quote: Prices what we have today, I mean in this Q2, I think most likely they will continue. But Q3 onwards, prices will go. And this is a regular pattern over years.

items.statement: India's manganese ore consumption expected to exceed 11 million tons by 2030 per National Steel Policy
items.quote: By 2030, it is envisaged to exceed 11 mi llion tons as per National Steel Policy

items.statement: Gujarat JV with GMDC identified 9.51 million tons of manganese ore resources, potential 2 lakh tons production starting FY26
items.quote: In Gujarat, I can share that we have explored, and we have identified about 9.51 million tons of manganese ore. Now based on the joint venture signing and then getting clearances perhaps the starting year we can say another 2 lakh tons, maybe next year there is '25-'26 but potential is 9.5

items.statement: No major impact from Supreme Court ruling on state mining taxes; no liability from Maharashtra or Madhya Pradesh state governments
items.quote: As far as the Sup reme Court decision is concerned, it is about the power of the states. The royalties are taxed or not. Royalty is not a tax. And if the state governments are imposing certain taxes, those taxes have to be paid since 2005, in the next 12 years. So, in case of MOIL, there are no taxes with respect to state governments. So, there is no liability from the state government

items.statement: Employee cost reset expected around 2027 due to pay scale revision
items.quote: That will be around 2027 or so.

items.statement: Exploration target of 1 lakh metres for FY25, added 7.98 million tons resources in FY24
items.quote: We are targeting aroun d 1 lakh metres to be explored and further we will add to our reserves and resources in the current financial year

items.statement: Targeting environmental clearance for 5 million tons by 2030 to support 3.5 million tons production
items.quote: By 2030, we are targeting environmental clearance for 5 million tons or 50 lakh tons, so that we can achieve our envisaged target of 3.5 million tons.

items.statement: Five new shafts planned across mines to support production growth
items.quote: So we have, and if you understand the language of mining engineers, that is number of shafts to be added. So it is under process, but we have decided on 5 shafts to be installed in different mines.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve from Q2 and surpass FY24 levels for full FY25
items.quote: it is expected that now from Q2, the margins will increase and it will surpass on Y-o-Y basis for FY25, the margin will surpass FY24.

items.statement: Order book of more than 50 MW captive projects, majority to be executed in FY25
items.quote: On the EP C front, we have very healthy order book for more than 50 megawatt of captive projects

items.statement: Evaluating investment opportunities in IPP segment including PM Kusum and C&I group captive projects
items.quote: We are looking for the investment opportunities as we have entered the IPP segment. We are evaluating the opportunities as and when like PM Kusum is one of the promising opportunity for investment.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of INR30 crore equity for INR150 crore PM Kusum IPP project with UGVCL PPA
items.quote: The purpose for going for QIP is to get an equity for investing into PM KUSUM projects where we have one project worth 26.56 megawatt and then the PPA with UGVCL. So the overall project size is INR150 crores, approximately INR150 crores. And for that, we have raised INR30 crores as an equity

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 5.58% vs 7.72% YoY due to salary, interest costs and high working capital orders
items.quote: Though the EBITDA margin contracted to 5.58 compared to 7.72 in Q1 FY24 due to investment in growth initiatives

items.statement: Solar panel prices stabilized in Q1 FY25 after volatility in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Q1 FY25 is steady. The prices of solar panel are steady and the volume is normally we are into capex.

items.statement: Solar sector growing at breakneck pace; PM Surya Ghar Yojana and state policies driving demand
items.quote: the solar energy sector is growing at a very breakneck pace. And the deployment of solar power in the country is rising exponentially.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 30% residential rooftop, 70% C&I, government and distribution business
items.quote: our rooftop, residential rooftop is around 30% of our revenue. And our commercial and industrial segment with government business and distribution business is contributing balance 70%.

items.statement: Informatics rating withdrawn after SEBI/RBI intervention; company did not engage for debt rating
items.quote: Ultimately, we complained to SEBI and RBI and after intervention for RBI and SEBI, Informatics has dropped our rating.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 90-100 days; working capital facility ~INR50 crore at 9.35% avg interest
items.quote: Current working capital cycle is roughly 90 to 100 days. Depending on the project, it may vary. But average current working capital cycle is around 90 to 100 days.

items.statement: Promoter stake ~72.8% pre-QIP, expected to marginally reduce to ~71.5-72% post-QIP
items.quote: before QIP, promoter stake was approximately 72.8%. With QIP, it will, I have not exact numbers, but it will marginally reduce to around 71.5% or 72%.

items.statement: Lucknow office operational for 4 months; Pune office to start within 1-2 months
items.quote: Lucknow office is operational and it is operational since last four months. And we are slowly and gradually gaining good orders from Lucknow office. Pune office is under process and soon it will be within a month or two, it will start operating

items.statement: FY25 revenue target INR305 crore (INR80 crore India, INR220 crore UAE)
items.quote: Revenue for '24-'25 yearly is INR80 crores for India operation and INR220 crores for UAE operation.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue expected INR63-65 crore
items.quote: And next quarter, this is the current quarter, Q2, we are expecting around INR63 crores to INR65 crores.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue expected around INR70-80 crore
items.quote: So, third quarter will be, we are expecting around, 75 to 80 Cr. Around 70 Cr.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target INR400 crore with same capacity
items.quote: And the next year, we are targeting around INR400 crores turnover with the same capacity.

items.statement: UAE plant to reach 100% capacity utilization in FY25-26
items.quote: In FY25 -26, we will be able to capture 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Total UAE capex invested INR105 crore including acquisition and working capital
items.quote: Total capex what we had invested in UAE is around INR105 crores, which includes the acquisition cost and the working capital together.

items.statement: Maintenance capex budgeted at 1.5-2% of turnover annually
items.quote: And maintenance is our, around 1.5% to 2% of the turnover, which we budget every year.

items.statement: Two acquisition proposals under discussion in India, may conclude this quarter
items.quote: Right now, there is no such expansion as we are filling our capacity. But definitely, once the demand will grow and the market size enlarge and we have a targeted turnover and targeted EBITDA naturally, we will expand.

items.statement: UAE order book ~40 million AED (75% UAE, 25% GCC/Africa); India confirmed project order book INR25 crore deliverable in 5-6 months
items.quote: The order book of UAE is around 40 million AED. And in India, it is like always month -on-month, the order book is there. But particularly for India, the project which we confirmed for supply of the glass and to be manufactured, there is around INR25 crores as on today.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 15-16% for FY25; UAE already at 15% EBITDA; India Q1 at 13.81% due to strike impact
items.quote: UAE market, we are already at 15 % EBITDA as on date also. India this quarter, as I said that because of that production loss, the margin were dipped by around 2% on EBITDA level. But average EBITDA is around 13.81 %, which is close to 14 %.

items.statement: Peak capacity EBITDA margin potential 17-19% (2-3% above current target)
items.quote: Right now, this year we are targeting around 15 % to 16% EBITDA. And maybe at the full potential, we can increase more by 2% to 3%.

items.statement: Selling price pressure from semi-organized competition; brand commands slight premium
items.quote: And because of this competitive environment, there is always a little bit of the selling price pressure. And we have also certain semi -organized competitions, where always there is a pressure on the pricing, though with our respectable brand, we have little bit of margin over competition.

items.statement: Architectural glass industry growing 35% CAGR driven by mandatory conversion from float glass and infrastructure growth
items.quote: Glass industry, the architectural glass is growing by 35% and the float glass industry is growing by around 12% to 15% compounding.

items.statement: Bulletproof glass sample under testing; UAE test certificate expected October, European certification by December; designer glass, ceramic frit to add margin
items.quote: Bulletproof glass, we already have a sample manufactured at our UAE plant and the same is under testing. So, we will be getting a local test certificate first in the first phase around in October. Then after we will further go for an European standard certification which generally takes three months.

items.statement: Key risk: real estate slowdown in India/UAE as 90% sales from architectural glass for commercial/residential buildings
items.quote: One key risk, if the economy of India and UAE can reduce, if the real estate can have the impact. Because our majority sale is coming around 90% from the real estate, architectural glasses for the commercial building, residential building.

items.statement: Acquisitions to be funded via debt-equity mix; will not increase interest burden significantly
items.quote: the debt and equity ratio we are expecting? Management: It's like again, once, we freeze on the valuation, then how the valuation payment structure are made, then we will decide. But yes, we will not, go more on the interest burden

items.statement: H2 FY25 expected to be 20-25% higher than H1 FY25; full-year FY25 growth will be below the previously budgeted 37%
items.quote: H1, which will close in September, we believe that H2 should be at least 20 or 25% higher than the H1, what we will close.

items.statement: Capex budget for FY25 under review and may be reduced from planned levels
items.quote: we are contemplating right now, we are doing each and every monitoring of the Capex which we have planned for this year and we may come with the reduction in our budgeted Capex plan for FY24-25

items.statement: European customers deferred orders due to high dealer inventory, US interest rates, and EV transition uncertainty; recovery expected post-August holidays
items.quote: are witnessing that there has been sudden reduction in customer orders because there has been huge inventory at dealer site and this most of the inventory reduction, I won't name the customers but most of our customers who have huge operations in the United States because of course the plants might be in Europe but they're higher customer base is

items.statement: EV demand volatility causing order cancellations and delays; customers lack new ICE/hybrid platforms after focusing on EV; US election and interest rate uncertainty
items.quote: consumers are not sure maybe should they go for hybrid, should they go for any other, the hydrogen is also being talked, so that is where I believe some of our projects did not pick up for which we have invested recently.

items.statement: RACL will still grow but at a reduced pace compared to past 35-30% growth
items.quote: RACL will still grow, but maybe not at the same pace where we were growing past three years and you know, pace of growth may change for growth will happen.

items.statement: Second half should be 10-20% better than first half
items.quote: I think the second-half should be ten 20% better than that.

items.statement: Revisiting and likely deferring non-critical capex; revised budget targeted by AGM
items.quote: We are in process of revisiting that CapEx budget. Since the as we have explained that European players are now opening up from the holidays, we are targeting to put up the revised CapEx budget contemplating to revive put up the revised CapEx budget by the AGM which we are planning next.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduction target for FY25; repayments exceed new borrowings
items.quote: Our target is that every year our repayments would be, yeah more than the more than the additional debt So that is also that those plans are already in place.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 22% currently; aspiration 20-23% maintained despite domestic mix
items.quote: If we are having 25% of EBIDTA even now we had a EBIDTA margin of 22%. It's not that we have. Gone upside down, we our beta margins are gone 3% if you see better in industry in India every time margin or not even 15%.

items.statement: European customers on holiday in July-August; real demand picture expected in 2-3 weeks after they return
items.quote: Eventually next two weeks will really give us a clear picture. Which way that the remaining months of the year have to go?

items.statement: Some customers cancelled/deferred orders due to inventory correction; one customer went from 4-month cancellation to restarting at reduced volume next month
items.quote: They said cancelling all orders for next four months and that is the kind of hustle we immediate. I mean the worry we immediately had. But then we went there, we understood the issue. They said there has been inventory correction.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility (military order hold, Red Sea crisis) causing demand volatility and inventory pile-up
items.quote: Suddenly these geopolitical things are really troubling. A lot of volatility. But I personally feel as vacation time is over, people are coming back, then they will be giving us a real stable demand for next one year at least.

items.statement: Domestic business growing with new substantial order (same product as European customer) and FCC India mass production started; margins between export and typical domestic
items.quote: This business is not very low margin business. This is actually a product which we are already producing for overseas, European customer, same product almost is going to adopted in the Indian motorcycle.

items.statement: ZF India sourcing plan intact despite short-term correction; China+1 and Europe FTA tailwinds expected
items.quote: India still remains their favourite country for sourcing. They have a big office, they're expanding their team and all that.

items.statement: May raise funds (preference shares/QIP) at right time for strategic decisions; not immediate
items.quote: These are all strategic surprise. Thanks for your message. But definitely these are our strategic decisions and yes, at the right time, the right decision will be on a take.

items.statement: Capacity utilisation currently 65-70%; peak 80-85% with given weeks
items.quote: In general we are right now operating with of course the reduced volumes we have around 65 to 70%.

items.statement: Solar captive power started July 20; expected saving ~1 crore annually on 1.4 crore equity investment
items.quote: I think its 1 Crore, because this this year we started only in July. We are 20th July, our captive power offsite generation started. So this year it will be lesser, but otherwise one crore will be the actual saving minimum at least.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 25% to 30% for FY25
items.quote: Despite a little slower in Q1, we are confident of achieving revenue growth in the range of 25% to 30% for FY '25.

items.statement: Order inflow target of INR11,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: On the order book side, we have set a target of INR11,000 crores for the financial year 24- 25.

items.statement: Order backlog of INR57,793 crores as of 12th August 2024
items.quote: The order backlog as of 12th August '24 is around INR57,793 crores.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book excluding 2 MDOs stands at INR18,115 crores
items.quote: If we exclude the 2 MDOs, the unexecuted order book stands at INR18,115 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 12.1% in Q1 FY25 from 12% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin has gone up from 12% in Q1 FY '24 to 12.1% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: MDO margins expected to improve after FY26-27, currently around 15% to 16%
items.quote: Until that time, it will be around 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Tracking INR75,000 crores of opportunities with hardcore opportunities of INR20,000-25,000 crores
items.quote: We are tracking about INR75,000 crores of opportunities and there are hardcore opportunities of nearly INR20,000 crores, INR25,000 crores.

items.statement: O&M revenue grew 52% YoY to INR341 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: O&M revenue of INR341 crores against INR224 crores in corresponding period last year, a registered growth of 52%.

items.statement: Civil business revenue grew 13% YoY to INR557 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Civil business, including railway, mining, water distribution contributed INR557 crores against INR493 crores in Q1 FY '24, an increase of 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: KBP MDO expected to break ground by end of September or beginning of October
items.quote: By end of September, beginning of October is when we expect to break ground, start the overburden activity.

items.statement: Supreme Court mine tax judgment will not impact MDO offtake due to contract clauses
items.quote: This is not going to impact the offtake at all. If it's going to impact the offtake, there are clauses that protect the offtake, as per the contract agreement.

items.statement: Overseas O&M revenue increased 27% YoY in Q1, expected to continue for 4-5 years
items.quote: Overseas O&M has increased compared to last year Q1 to this year's Q1, overseas O&M has increased by close to 27%. Revenue in this trend is expected to continue for the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to normalize to 26%-27% in FY25
items.quote: We are on 26% to 27% for this year.

items.statement: Secured orders worth INR1,746 crores so far in FY25
items.quote: So far, this financial year, the company has secured orders worth of INR1,746 crores.
